The findings were deliberately left un-unified, because inferring an absent apostrophe would merge genuine plurals into possessives and hide real cases. Proposed: an artifact-level fill sanity check that reports a filled book with zero apostrophes across dozens of nodes as ONE fill defect, so a transcription fault is attributed to the artifact rather than spread across whichever rule reads that text next; then re-derive PN-1's noise floor from a corpus without the affected artifacts, since the published 2.97-per-100 figure is an upper bound. Second, smaller caveat on the same figure, recorded in validator/naming.py's docstring: the out/ corpus predates ADR-023 and carries no sentinels, so the HERO-sentinel hero exemption fires on no book there and every book reports its own protagonist. 4b unscheduled UW-C395 AL-644: A prose defect in a published book has no in-place remedy, and the only exit from published removes the book from the reader. api/node_edit.py permits an edit only while a storybook is in_review or needs_revision, never published or archived; publishing/state_machine.py's LEGAL_TRANSITIONS offers exactly one transition out of PUBLISHED (ARCHIVE to ARCHIVED) and ARCHIVED is absorbing. Concrete instance: sk_cave_of_echoes v1, 64 nodes, one reader mid-book and two assignments, needs a three-word gloss on Biscuit (named in 64 of 64 nodes, "dog" in none) and a consistency pass over 23 nodes that write Maya as a literal while 41 nodes carry a {~HERO:Maya~} sentinel, so a personalized reader currently meets both her own name and Maya's in the same book. The immutability guarantee is correct and must not be weakened: a book a child is reading must not change under her. Owner decision this row carries: how a published book's prose defect is remediated at all. Candidate shapes are a REVISE transition from PUBLISHED to NEEDS_REVISION that keeps the published version readable until a successor is approved, or a documented supersede-and-reassign procedure that never leaves a reader with nothing. Explicitly out of scope: widening node_edit's status guard to mutate a published blob in place. 4b decision UW-C396 AL-645: retrofit_personalization.py cannot see a hero-name occurrence the fill invented beyond the skeleton's slot references, and reports success anyway. Dry run against production for sk_cave_of_echoes v1: 41/42 tokens reinserted, eligible=True, the one miss naming n_open, a node absent from the deployed blob. The same blob carried 41 literal "Maya" occurrences across 23 other nodes with no slot behind them, so a personalizing family would have met their child's name in 41 nodes and "Maya" in 23. Repaired for this book on 2026-08-27 by wrapping the residual occurrences outside existing sentinels (round-trip verified via strip_model_sentinels, manifest re-derived: 41 nodes / 78 occurrences to 64 / 119). Residual this row carries: the sweep itself is unchanged. Proposed: after the skeleton-anchored pass, wrap residual bare occurrences of the pinned default_binding value under the same round-trip invariant, or emit their count as a coverage finding so a half-personalized book stops reading as a finished one. Also worth a sweep: how many of the other 14 books the retrofit touched are in the same partial state, since the sweep's own output cannot distinguish them from complete ones. 4b unscheduled UW-C397 AL-646: import_filled_story is unusable as a repair path for any book that predates a gate tightening, because it tests blocked absolutely rather than comparing against the stored version. The published sk_cave_of_echoes v1 fails today's gate on one ERROR, PL-25 opening: first decision is 1 node(s) in, under the band '8-11' floor 2; PL-25's floor escalation merged in v0.67.0, after the book was imported. So re-importing a corrected copy requires either authoring a new opening node (changing a story a child is mid-way through, and needing fresh moderation) or bypassing the deterministic gate on child-facing content. Both were refused on 2026-08-27 and the repair was done in place instead (AL-647). Proposed: a repair mode that admits a blob whose gate finding multiset is no worse than the stored version's, the same comparison retrofit_personalization.py's invariant 5 already makes; for this repair that comparison was exactly PN-1: -1 and nothing else. Until it exists, document in-place repair as the only route for a pre-tightening book. Related but distinct from UW-C395, which asks for a sanctioned state-machine exit from published; this row is about the import gate, and either one alone leaves the other gap open. 4b unscheduled UW-C398 AL-655: A stored moderation_report has no single agreed way to answer "was every node screened", and the obvious formula manufactures phantom gaps. A Finding carries node_id (one representative node, for display anchoring) and node_ids (every node a batch-wide finding covers); reconciling pass_counts.safety against node_id alone under-counts by up to review_batch_size - 1 per batch finding. During the 2026-08-26 re-moderation coverage audit this read three books (sk_sunken_signal, sk_sunspire_ascent, sk_thornwood_trial) as silently missing 8 screened nodes each, when the pipeline had in fact reported every one of them through a HIGH-severity structural=True flag carrying concern="reviewer_unavailable". Ship scripts/moderation_coverage.py as the one reconciliation of record (stage-1 sources, node_ids or [node_id], asserted equal to aggregate.nodes_reviewed) so a genuine coverage hole and an auditor's misread stop being indistinguishable. 4b unscheduled UW-C399 AL-656: A safety-review batch is discarded whole when the reviewer omits a single node, costing 8 nodes of coverage per omission. Observed live on sk_ashfall_expedition 2026-08-26: the reviewer returned 7 well-formed, unambiguously attributable verdicts for an 8-node batch, dropping n_b28_2_2. _parse_batch_verdicts refuses partial attribution by design (stages.py docstring, design doc 2.3) and the whole batch fail-safes, which is the correct safety posture and must be preserved. Narrow the remedy to the id-set mismatch branch only: re-review the missing ids on the single-node path, which is documented byte-identical to unbatched behavior, and merge; fall back to whole-batch fail-safe if the retry also fails. Truncation and decode failures keep the existing all-or-nothing handling, since no verdict in those responses is trustworthy. 4b unscheduled UW-C400 AL-657: Determine whether a fail-safed safety batch is reproducible on its content before spending any re-run budget on closing coverage holes. sk_thornwood_trial re-moderated twice produced a rewritten report whose reviewer judgments moved, while the reviewer_unavailable finding named the same 8 node ids both times; _chunks partitions consecutively so batch boundaries are stable run to run. Test with sk_sunken_signal (32 nodes, cheapest affected book) and compare the fail-safed id set. If deterministic, re-running never closes these holes and the remedy is UW-C399's per-node retry or a reduced batch size for the offending chunk; if not, re-running is sound. Blocks the re-run plan for sk_sunken_signal, sk_sunspire_ascent, and sk_ashfall_expedition. 4b unscheduled UW-C401 AL-658: aggregate.nodes_reviewed reads 0 on every hard-blocked moderation report, including books whose safety stage screened every node. Verified across the full 31-book catalog on 2026-08-26: 8 of 8 hard-blocked reports report 0, all 23 others are correct. pipeline.py assigns the field past the last stage so early returns keep the default, which correctly prevents claiming coverage a short-circuited run never had, but overloads one field with two meanings. sk_sunken_temple (blocked after 550 of 550 screened, pass_counts.safety=520 beside it) is indistinguishable from sk_cave_of_echoes (blocked before review, genuinely 0). Split the concerns: persist the nodes actually screened at each stage exit, plus an explicit review_complete boolean for stage completion. Consumers reading the aggregate as a denominator (api/node_edit.py, moderation dashboard) currently get a false zero. 4b unscheduled UW-C402 AL-659: a moderation unknown_slot hard block does not say which side of the contract/blob pair is wrong, so the intuitive remedy is backwards half the time. sk_vanishing_orchard blocked on 216 <global> violations; annotating the apparently-missing HERO in all 10 under-declaring contracts was rejected by ThemeContract on 6 of them and fixed no live defect on the other 4. The discriminator is a catalog-wide declared-vs-observed join: 12 of 13 sentinel-bearing books are consistent and exactly 1 is not, which identifies over-stamping rather than under-declaration. Emit both sets in the failure message (declared={} observed={HERO}), and add an at-rest catalog consistency check to the sweep tooling so divergence is found without needing a hard block. Scans must use SENTINEL_RE ({~SLOT:value~}); a {{SLOT}} probe silently returns zero. 4b unscheduled UW-C403 AL-660: generation can mark a version personalization_eligible and stamp sentinels for a slot its own theme contract refuses to declare personalizable. the-vanishing-orchard is the only contract of 47 with _FULL slots, and its opening line is The last bus left {~HERO:Rowan~} Ashby: the surname sits outside the sentinel, so a personalized copy would read "Kate Ashby". PERSONALIZATION_FIELDS has no protagonist_full_name, so no annotation can fix it. The blob nonetheless carries 216 HERO sentinels and personalization_eligible=True. No reader is affected (slot_bindings derives from the contract, so the slot is unbound and resolves to Rowan), but blob and contract disagree at rest. Gate the stamping path on the same invariant the model enforces, and lint the catalog for a _FULL companion beside a personalizable first-name slot. De-stamping the published blob is blocked by ADR-005 immutability and is an owner decision. 4b unscheduled UW-C404 AL-661: edit_node re-gates the whole blob, so a pre-existing unrelated gate error blocks every targeted repair and the rejection blames the edit. Repairing sk_sunken_temple's single blocked node failed with edited passage failed the validation gate; run_fill_gate on the unmodified blob returned the identical single PL-25 error, proving the edit innocent and the book already failing. Without gating the pre-edit artifact first, the obvious response is to rewrite correct prose until something passes, which cannot converge. Split the post-edit findings against a pre-edit baseline and return only edit-introduced findings as the rejection reason, reporting pre-existing ones separately as a book-level blocker. 4b unscheduled UW-C405 AL-662: PL-25 is structural but edit_node is prose-only, so the word-equivalence relaxation is the only reachable fix for a book in review, and it forces the opening node past its own advisory ceiling. sk_sunken_temple's n_start is itself the first decision (depth 1 against a floor of 2); inserting a choiceless establishing node is the fix the rule wants and edit_node forbids it. The relaxation needs most_words >= 2 * 65 = 130 in a node whose advisory ceiling is 90 and hard maximum is 145, a 15-word-wide target that trades a PL-25 error for a words-per-node warning. Report the band's word-equivalence threshold and per-node maximum in the PL-25 message, and allow a review-stage structural insert. 4b unscheduled UW-C406 AL-663: scripts/remoderate_books.py collapses failed, blocked, excluded, timed_out and not_attempted into one sys.exit(<str>), always exit 1, so a retry loop cannot distinguish a permanent hard block from a retryable rollback. sweep.sh retried sk_vanishing_orchard three times in 15 seconds against a verdict that cannot change without a prose edit, re-spending an LLM review pass each time. The exit code was designed as a human attention signal and reused as a machine retry signal. Give blocked and excluded a distinct exit code, break the sweep loop on it, and add a --json summary. Same shape recurs in moderation/classifiers.py::_run_openai, which catches base httpx.HTTPError so a permanent 401 retries like a transient 429; fix with the _TRANSIENT_STATUS split the three generation providers already use. DONE 2026-08-27: both halves landed on fix/published-slot-contract-false-block. db03e57d splits the exit codes (1 = retryable: failed/timed_out/not_attempted; 3 = needs a human: blocked/excluded; 3 rather than 2 because argparse owns 2 for usage errors) and breaks the sweep loop on 3. 0a2a05b3 fixes the classifiers.py recurrence by moving the retry decision onto the exception (ClassifierUnavailable(retryable=, disables_classifier=)) with an httpx.HTTPStatusError arm ordered ahead of the (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) arm it subclasses; a credential rejection now latches the circuit on the first node instead of re-proving itself on every remaining one. Both keyword defaults are the safe answer, so raise sites that predate the change keep retrying. Verified by mutation: flipping retryable in either direction, replacing the disabled latch with pass, and latching on every status each kill at least one test; the 5xx test asserts WHICH nodes were attempted, since a call count cannot separate three retries of one node from one attempt at each of three. now done UW-C407 AL-664: one failed review batch removes 8 nodes from safety coverage and downgrades the book's hard block to a soft flag, so an incompletely-reviewed book reports as a successful pass. stages.py:752 raises the shortfall as a structural=True/HIGH/reviewer_unavailable finding whose verdict is Verdict.FLAG; report.py::has_hard_block is any(verdict is BLOCK), so the flag clears the hard block, has_soft_flag becomes true, remoderate_books exits 0 and the sweep prints soft-flagged, review when convenient. Established on sk_sunken_temple with prose identity proven from pipeline_event (only two node_edited rows exist in the whole table, both at 12:20:47): the 12:21 and 01:52 passes had full coverage and BOTH hard-blocked on disjoint nodes, while the 13:55 pass with 8 unreviewed nodes cleared the block. 5 of 31 current reports admit unreviewed nodes and all 5 read hard_block=False: sk_ashfall_expedition 16, sk_harrowstone_keep 8, sk_sunken_temple 8, sk_sunspire_ascent 8, sk_thornwood_trial 8; the exact recurring 8 is review_batch_size (config.py:650), so this is batch-granular, not node-granular. Add coverage_complete to ModerationReport and make the gating predicate false-safe on incomplete review; fall back to per-node review when a batch response is unusable so one bad response costs 1 node rather than 8; give remoderate_books a distinct exit class for reviewed incompletely. Same family as the soft-stage fail-safe shape already tracked, one layer up: node-level fail-safe composing into book-level fail-open. now done UW-C408 AL-665: the moderation reviewer pins no sampling parameters and the stored report records no model provenance, so a safety verdict is a sample rather than a measurement and cannot be attributed after the fact. openrouter.py:317 sends only model/messages/max_tokens: no temperature, seed or top_p. The review model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (config.py:606) has no ENDPOINT_PINS entry, so endpoint_pin_for returns (), the body omits provider, and successive passes may be served by different backends at different quantizations. build_openrouter_leg's own #ASSUME already states that consequence, but only for cost. A persisted moderation_report carries no model, provider or endpoint field, which is why the 2026-07-21 mock-reviewer run left no detectable signature and had to be inferred from finding counts. Pin temperature=0 (plus a seed where honoured), add the review model to ENDPOINT_PINS, and persist model/provider/endpoint/sampling into the report beside reviewer_independent. Pinning will move verdicts catalog-wide: the first pinned sweep is a new baseline, not a comparison against the unpinned history. 4b done UW-C409 AL-666: editing a shell script while an instance of it is running corrupts that run and misreports the faulting line. Bash reads a script from a byte offset, so an edit that changes the file's length makes the running shell resume mid-token; a 14:16 edit to sweep.sh made a run started at ~13:56 execute the fragment nswer out of a comment on line 67 and report it against line 72, and silently dropped the sweep's final report block. bash -n afterwards is clean and proves nothing; the mtime-versus-start-time comparison is the only diagnostic. Have the sweep runner cp the script to a run-scoped path under its log directory and execute the copy, which immunises the run and records what was actually executed beside its output. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-C410 AL-668: coverage_complete is the absence of gap findings, so a run that reviews nothing reports complete coverage. report.py:346 sets coverage_complete = not has_coverage_gap, and has_coverage_gap (report.py:271) scans findings for a concern in COVERAGE_GAP_CONCERNS, which only exists when a batch response was unusable. When the pipeline aborts BEFORE the safety pass there is no such finding: sk_ninth_hand hard-blocked on entry_contract_unrecoverable + version_contract_band_missing in 7s and persisted coverage_complete=true with aggregate.nodes_reviewed=0, having read 0 of 746 nodes. The hard block is what stopped this being a live fail-open, so the verdict was right and only the coverage claim is false; but it defeats every consumer that reads coverage_complete as evidence, and it defeated the re-moderation sweep's completion oracle, which would have skipped the book permanently on resume. Make coverage a POSITIVE assertion: require nodes_reviewed > 0, ideally equal to the version's node count, or replace the bool with a tri-state so not_attempted and complete cannot collapse. Amended 2026-08-27: nodes_reviewed > 0 is NOT a sound substitute on its own, per the already-open AL-658 / UW-C401. That counter encodes STAGE completion, not a node count, so it reads 0 for every hard-blocked book however much was screened; requiring it would trade this fail-open for a false alarm on every legitimate block. Confirmed again on 2026-08-27 by the 21-book sweep, where the only two zero-counter rows were opposite cases: sk_ninth_hand (pass_counts {}, 1 finding, source pipeline, 7s, nothing read) and sk_harrowstone_keep (pass_counts {safety: 535}, 26 findings from llm_safety and openai across 22 node_ids, 5837s, fully screened then blocked on content). Fix UW-C401 first, or gate on pass_counts rather than on nodes_reviewed. Same family as UW-C407 one layer out: book-level fail-safe composing into a catalog-level false all-clear. 4b unscheduled UW-C411 AL-671: a gate that reads an optional field cannot see a construction site that omits it. The narrow concern set is now derived from the broader one, closing the specific hole, but nothing prevents the next fail-safe Finding from being built without a concern=. Add a suite-wide test asserting that every Finding construction with structural=True and severity HIGH carries a concern in MOCK_MODERATED_CONCERNS or COVERAGE_GAP_CONCERNS, and consider making concern required on that shape rather than optional. 4b unscheduled UW-C412 AL-672: gh api .../contents truncates at 1MB and returns 200, so a tail over it reports a wrong maximum id. Both ledgers are past or near the limit. Add a --max-id mode to scripts/check_lessons_log.py and scripts/check_work_linkage.py so the highest id in use comes from the parser that already reads every row, and record the git show origin/main:<path> rule where the renumber procedure is documented. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-C413 AL-673: the register's declared header has five columns and 408 of 410 cluster-C rows have four, so column 3 holds Phase under an "ADR" heading. Markdown pads short rows so the table renders, and the linkage checker parses by id rather than by arity. Normalise the rows to the header or change the header to the dominant shape, and have check_work_linkage.py assert column arity per cluster. 4b unscheduled UW-C414 AL-674: the RAD gate grandfathers citations, including on #CRITICAL markers, and treats a multi-test citation as satisfied piecemeal. A safety-gating marker cited a test that existed nowhere and passed for weeks on a baseline row. Make check_rad_citations.py refuse a baseline row for any citation attached to a #CRITICAL marker, and require every test named by one marker to resolve. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-C415 AL-675: moderation_report_unusable()'s legacy discriminator rests on deployment history rather than on the schema. It infers report vintage from the presence of summary.coverage_complete, which holds only because no intermediate revision of this branch ever persisted a report; a cherry-pick or a replay invalidates it. Add an explicit schema-version key to the persisted report and read that instead, retiring the inference and its #EDGE. 4b unscheduled UW-C416 AL-678: a per-agent control cannot classify a finding as pre-existing while a concurrent agent's edit stands in the same tree. Two basedpyright errors were reported as pre-existing on a file-scoped revert; both named a symbol absent at the merge base. Record the merge-base evidence rule (git show origin/main:<path>) in the concurrent-session guidance, and require a dispatched agent to cite it when it calls a finding pre-existing. CI hygiene unscheduled

docs.title: Cluster D: untracked GitHub issues
docs.text:
roadmap.md lines 197-199 assert that open issues "remain accurately tracked" in the debt register. That claim is false: the debt register cites 9 issue numbers, 6 still open, against 48 open issues as of 2026-08-03. The 34 issues below appear in no other planning document by number or by description, so this cluster is their only phase home.

Adding a row here is now a judgement call rather than a gate. scripts/check_work_linkage.py once carried a --check-issue-orphans flag requiring every open GitHub issue to be cited under docs/planning/ or labelled unplanned, plus a --check-issues flag resolving each cited number against the API. Both were retired: they ran only in CI, because they needed network access and gh auth that the pre-commit hook deliberately does not have, so the two gates enforced different contracts and a green local run proved nothing about the stricter one. The recurring cost also outgrew the return, most visibly when the workflow's own drift-alert issue became an uncited open issue and failed the gate that filed it. What remains is the offline linkage contract, which every row in this table is still bound by.

ID Issues Theme Phase Status UW-D01 #249, #250, #251, #253, #254 Device-auth and principal hardening (existence oracle, type invariants, token audiences, double-revoke, shared secret helper) 5 unscheduled UW-D02 #252 expires_at on device_grant so active-devices excludes ghosts 4b unscheduled UW-D03 #255 Device-auth doc-diagram refresh and test hygiene CI hygiene unscheduled UW-D04 #137 All error conditions render one generic retryable error (naive-UX F1) 4b unscheduled UW-D05 #144 Stage-0 classifiers handle NaN and Infinity asymmetrically 5 unscheduled UW-D06 #347 Catalog import: pre-upload quality gating and verdict_parse_failed under mock 5 unscheduled UW-D07 #63 storybook_version lacks a provider column, so provenance is unrecoverable 5 unscheduled UW-D08 #138 Pin the homelab backend-net subnet, narrow FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS 9 unscheduled UW-D09 #302, #383, #382, #364, #248 CI and release hygiene (mutation run failing, Codecov carryforward race, cast() narrowing, release re-verification, markdownlint debt) CI hygiene unscheduled UW-D10 #67 coverage.py zero hits for async handlers under CPython 3.12; probably obsolete after the 3.14 move CI hygiene verify UW-D11 #290 The scheduled real-backend nightly E2E is failing. Phase 5 tracks the capability; the failing run is uncited. 5 unscheduled UW-D12 #295 Python 3.14 residual: target-version = "py311", plus rollout steps 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 from the upgrade evaluation (Renovate lockstep, 3.14 in python-compatibility.yml, flip ci.yml to required, staged homelab deploy, post-flip cleanup) 5 unscheduled UW-D13 #221 A wrong or defaulted R2 bucket passes the covers-configured guard 7 unscheduled UW-D14 #187, #172 Promote api-tests to a required gate; Codecov Bundle Analysis blocked on Vite 8. Named in the capability register only. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-D15 #453 Family-scoped ADMIN_ACTOR_ROLE hardcodes audit dual-role owners as cross-family admins 5 unscheduled UW-D16 #74 Guardian console "Still processing" is inert for admins. Canonical with debt U2. 4b unscheduled UW-D17 #71 App-wide rate-limit policy for polling endpoints. The mechanism already exists: middleware/security.py::RateLimitMiddleware applies one Redis-backed per-client-IP limit across every route. Check whether polling routes (reading state, generation status, notifications) need their own tier rather than sharing the global bucket, and close the issue if the single tier is the intended policy. 5 verify UW-D18 #535 3 linux-libc-dev kernel-header CVEs, 2 of them fixable by a base-image refresh. DONE: CVE-2026-64530 and CVE-2026-64531 were cleared on 2026-08-02 by the bump to 6.12.100-1+dhi0 and are in the Resolved Entries table; CVE-2026-63879 (no trixie fix) is now covered by the package-scoped acceptance rather than a per-CVE entry. Closed by the 2026-08-16 base-image CVE change on branch claude/trivy-base-image-cves-vixpcq: .trivy/ignore-policy.rego (+ trivy.yaml) and the consolidated docs/known-vulnerabilities.md entry. Issue #535 has no residual work and can be closed. 5 done UW-D19 #505 7 unfixed linux-libc-dev kernel-header CVEs with no Debian trixie fix. Superseded rather than fixed: all 7 are absorbed into the package-scoped acceptance, so they no longer need individual tracking, and the upstream blocker (no trixie-track fix) is unchanged. The remaining actionable item is the upstream ask that linux-libc-dev be dropped from the DHI runtime image, which is external:container-images only in routing: the mirror is disposition: mirror_only, so it is really an ask to Docker. Closed by the 2026-08-16 base-image CVE change on branch claude/trivy-base-image-cves-vixpcq: .trivy/ignore-policy.rego (+ trivy.yaml) and the consolidated docs/known-vulnerabilities.md entry. 5 done UW-D20 #542 Stage-1 reviewer passes prompt-injection corpus items E2/E3 at every batch size, so the injection gap is not a batch-tuning artifact and the PR #541 batch-size default cannot close it. From the moderation review redesign track. 5 unscheduled UW-D21 #552 renovate.json package rules that never fire. Another silent-gate failure: a rule matching nothing is indistinguishable from a rule with nothing to match, so the config looks configured while the dependency class it names goes ungoverned. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-D22 #571 e2e-staging is green by retry, not clean: the last spec's device-grant revoke fails its first attempt in every observed run and passes on retries: 1. The console's own banner proves the backend rejected the DELETE, and an identical helper call earlier in the tier passes first time, so it is position-dependent rather than a helper bug. Starts as CI hygiene because the first deliverable is diagnostic: the banner text cannot discriminate 429 from 401, 5xx, or a dropped connection, so the actual status must be captured before a cause can be named. If the 60 rpm/IP hypothesis confirms, the fix converges with UW-D17 (#71) in phase 5 and this row moves there. Green-with-retry does not close it. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-D23 #573 The weekly whole-corpus link check found at least one dead link in docs/, README.md, or CONTRIBUTING.md. Filed by link-check-full.yml, which scans ~100 third-party hosts, so confirm a link is actually dead before editing: a host that refuses HEAD or rate-limits the runner reads identically to rot. Related to UW-D26's standing problem, and to the reason that check was split out of the PR gate in the first place (#563). CI hygiene unscheduled UW-D24 #574 The weekly dependency-provenance report. It currently reports zero actionable transitive vulnerabilities and self-describes as a sticky marker that is updated rather than reopened, so it is a dashboard, not a defect: it stays open by design and closing it would only cause the next run to file a new one. The obligation is to read it each week and act when the count stops being zero, which is a practice rather than a deliverable. recurring unscheduled UW-D25 #575 The scheduled Planning Linkage check failed and filed this alert. Its cause was the #571 orphan, which UW-D22 above resolves, so this is very likely already fixed. To check: dispatch or wait for a scheduled planning-linkage.yml run after UW-D22 merges, confirm it is green, then close the issue. Nothing closes it automatically; the workflow's own text asks a human to. CI hygiene verify UW-D26 (no issue) Standing problem, not a defect in any one run, and the reason the three rows above exist at all. Scheduled workflows file ci-failure issues that are deduplicated by title but never auto-closed, and an open uncited issue is an orphan, so every bot alert fails the very gate that files it. #575 is the pure case: the linkage check filed an issue that then made the linkage check fail. The considered fixes were to label bot issues unplanned at filing time, to exempt ci-failure in --check-issue-orphans, or to close the issue from the workflow on a green run. Decided instead to remove both issue-facing checks (--check-issues and --check-issue-orphans): tying every open issue to the phase plan was a good idea that cost more than it returned, and an offline checker is also one that the pre-commit hook and CI can run identically. Removal landed in PR #576; the checker now makes no network call and the intro to this cluster records why. CI hygiene done UW-D27 #558 Automated database backup and a tested restore drill. docs/operations/runbook.md section 6 stated plainly none existed in this repository. scripts/backup_database.py + .github/workflows/supabase-backup.yml close the backup half (daily supabase db dump, AES-256-GCM encryption, tiered R2 upload with GFS lifecycle rules, and failure alerting); the restore procedure is documented but not yet drilled against a live project, so this stays open until that drill runs. Canonical with the roadmap's Phase 5 "backups and a tested restore" line. 5 unscheduled UW-D28 #557 Alert on security events rather than only emitting them. PR #599 and PR #600 are both the emission side: #599 shaped and throttled the log events, #600 added the durable security_event table behind them. Neither wires a notification channel, so security-events.md section 6 still describes zero shipped alert rules and section 2's "Alert on" lines remain a specification. Three specifics the issue body predates: the rules live in homelab-infra, not this repo; security_event_write_failed needs its own alert-on-any-occurrence rule, because fail-open means a silent audit gap looks exactly like an absence of attacks; and the security_event table has no retention or purge mechanism at all, which is an ADR-018 gap the append-only trigger makes harder to close, not easier. Note the issue body cites UW-D19 as its register home, which is wrong: that ID is #505, the unfixed kernel-header CVEs. This row is the correct one. 5 unscheduled UW-D29 #601 Original finding, superseded below by PR #604; kept as the record of why this row exists. supabase/config.toml was committed but never deployed: supabase-staging.yml/supabase-production.yml run supabase db push (migrations) only, no config push step exists anywhere in .github/workflows/. Production's real [auth] policy (password requirements, rate limits, captcha) is whatever was last set by hand in the dashboard, unreviewable and undocumented, including the only throttle on the unauthenticated resetPasswordForEmail path. Previously deferred as design-spec follow-up 3 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-supabase-environments-pipeline-design.md pending CLI stability; supabase config push is confirmed supported at the pinned CLI version 2.109.1, so that reason no longer holds. The prerequisite blocker (production was adopted from an already-live project and its [auth] block had never been reconciled against config.toml) is cleared: both projects' live auth config were read from the Management API and diffed field by field against the file on 2026-08-04, and the diff was reviewed before anything was written. Every divergence ran in the loosening direction, confirming the checked-in file was a local-dev file rather than an aspirational policy. Delivered in PR #604: config.toml now carries the agreed policy (password floor 10 per NIST SP 800-63B, email confirmations on, OTP length 8, TOTP MFA on, a 60s email throttle via [auth.email].max_frequency, reauthentication required for password change). Note that [auth.rate_limit].email_sent is a different setting and is not live: it needs custom SMTP, tracked separately as UW-D30 plus [remotes.staging]/[remotes.production] blocks for the two genuinely per-environment fields, and config push runs in both deploy workflows between link and db push, with a log assertion that the expected [remotes.*] override actually loaded rather than leaving that check to a human reading the run log. Staging is deployed and verified against a pre-push snapshot with a delta of exactly the two intended fields. Production is wired but has never been dispatched, which is why this row stays at verify rather than closing: it sits behind the production GitHub Environment's required-reviewer gate, so the first production rollout is a human action rather than a merge side effect, and nothing else in the plan tracks that action. A row marked done here would be the only record, and it would say the work is finished when half of it has not run. Closed 2026-08-04: every step of that checklist ran. Staging deployed automatically on the merge of #604 (run 30933782746); production deployed by human-approved dispatch (run 30934654664) after a pre-push snapshot of all five surfaces. Both runs printed Loading config override: [remotes.<env>] and passed the fail-closed ref guard, and both reported API, DB and Storage already up to date, so the delta stayed confined to [auth] as designed. Production moved exactly four fields, established by diffing the Management API field by field against the snapshot rather than by reading the run log: password_min_length 6 to 10, security_update_password_require_reauthentication false to true, password_required_characters null to "" (equivalent), and uri_allow_list gaining https://cyo.williamshome.family/**. Nothing else on the auth surface moved and the other four surfaces were byte-identical. The three deliberate omissions held: Google OAuth still enabled with its client_id intact, captcha and HIBP left unmanaged rather than asserted off. Two things a future reader would otherwise rediscover. First, the staging run was not the zero-delta predicted: it applied secure_password_change false to true, a field tightened during review of #604 after staging had been reconciled by hand, which is git asserting itself over a manual setting rather than drift. Second, the reset-flow #VERIFY that gated this row's own risk has now been exercised against production and the feared deadlock is not real; see supabase/config.toml's marker for the evidence. Promotion procedure and the snapshot/restore recovery path: docs/guides/supabase-environments.md section 4. Follow-on: UW-D30. 5 done UW-D30 (no issue) No custom SMTP provider is configured on either Supabase project, so [auth.rate_limit].email_sent in supabase/config.toml is not deployed. Split out of UW-D29, which found it: the CLI sends rate_limit_email_sent only when [auth.email.smtp] is enabled, and smtp_host reads null on both project refs, so auth email goes through Supabase's built-in service under that service's own project-wide cap. The practical effect is that the value in the file is inert, and the only throttles actually protecting the unauthenticated resetPasswordForEmail path (frontend/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx) are smtp_max_frequency, set to 60s, plus the built-in cap, which is not ours to tune. A config value that looks like policy but is inert is worse than an absent one, so the file carries a #CRITICAL marker saying so until this is fixed. Also blocks any transactional email beyond the built-in service's deliverability and volume limits. To do: provision an SMTP provider, add [auth.email.smtp], then confirm the configured email_sent starts appearing in the Management API's rate_limit_email_sent. Related: leaked-password protection (password_hibp_enabled) is separately unavailable, returning HTTP 402 on the free plan and having no config.toml key at CLI 2.109.1; both are recorded in the file's [auth] comments. 5 unscheduled UW-D31 (no issue) 8 CVEs suppressed in .trivyignore with no entry in docs/known-vulnerabilities.md: perl-base (5), libsqlite3-0 (2), ncurses (1), all introduced undocumented by d1907a8 (PR #668). DONE 2026-08-17: all three entries written with per-package reachability analysis, known-vulnerabilities-baseline.toml deleted, and tests/unit/test_check_known_vulnerabilities.py::test_repository_carries_no_grandfathered_debt added so the baseline cannot quietly reappear. Two findings worth carrying forward: two of the perl CVEs are Critical (CVE-2026-8376, CVE-2026-42496) and were accepted silently for a week, and the two libsqlite3-0 CVEs are Medium, so they sit below the CRITICAL,HIGH scan threshold and their ignore entries suppress nothing today. Residual, deliberately not closed here: fix status came from Trivy's own Debian advisory records, not from an independent Debian tracker check, because that host is unreachable from cloud sessions; each entry says so and carries the re-verification as an open task. Tracked onward by #711 item 1. 5 done UW-D32 (no issue) Decide whether to adopt python-container-revisit.yml from ByronWilliamsCPA/.github v10.1.0. It runs a weekly full-scope scan and maintains one tracker issue via track_unfixed_cves.py, giving every unfixed CVE a first-seen and a due date. Deliberately NOT adopted on 2026-08-17: that is per-CVE enumeration, which is exactly what the linux-libc-dev consolidation removed, and our Rego policy filters those findings before the tracker would ever see them. It also needs issues: write on the caller. Revisit if the weekly Container Security run stops being a sufficient backstop, or if a second package ever needs package-scoped acceptance. Owner ruling needed on whether org uniformity outweighs the enumeration cost. 5 decision UW-D33 (no issue) tests/unit/test_trivy_ignore_policy.py::TestPolicyEvaluation is skipped whenever the trivy binary is absent, which is every CI unit-test run: no job installs it. The structural assertions still run and catch the three ways the policy silently becomes a no-op (wrong FixedVersion comparison, a second permissive ignore rule, a missing expiry), so the loss is the end-to-end tier only, which was verified locally against Trivy 0.70.0. Either install Trivy in the unit-test job or move this tier into the Container Security workflow, which already has the binary. Raised by Greptile on PR #725 against the tests/CLAUDE.md rule that a conditional skip carries a tracking reference. CI hygiene unscheduled

docs.title: Cluster F: test and quality hardening
docs.text:
From testing-review-2026-07-22.md, test-coverage-audit-2026-07-09.md, and test-traceability-matrix.md. Phase 5's generic "test ladder" line needs to become these named actions.

ID Item Phase Status UW-F01 C1 no behavioral safety evaluation: mocks only, a 13-item corpus, zero llm_eval tests in CI. Debt GS2 tracks the live adversarial run, not the suite. 5 unscheduled UW-F02 H1 foreign-key ON DELETE parity gap; the migration header falsely claims coverage 5 unscheduled UW-F03 H2 frontend hand-mirrored adapters bypass the generated client, with no OpenAPI-pinned test 5 unscheduled UW-F04 H3 mutmut enforces no kill-floor on PRs CI hygiene unscheduled UW-F05 H4 zero performance and load testing before Phase 9; perf markers are dead. Phase 5's "performance pass" needs teeth. 5 unscheduled UW-F06 M1 full-stack E2E never drives the RQ worker 5 unscheduled UW-F07 M2 schema parity omits policies, triggers, and functions 5 unscheduled UW-F08 M3 player-parity corpus is 3 traces 5 unscheduled UW-F09 M4 interrogate and pydoclint never run in CI CI hygiene unscheduled UW-F10 M5 coverage-combine verified on a subset only CI hygiene unscheduled UW-F11 M6 no rate-limit or CORS negative tests 5 unscheduled UW-F12 L1 through L6 (node_edit integration, a dead or True assertion, SimpleNamespace casts, index-predicate parity, 70 versus 80% thresholds, no @example seeds) CI hygiene unscheduled UW-F13 Coverage-audit batches A, B, C (backend floors, standards conformance, frontend Vitest). A branch test/coverage-gap-closure exists with no plan row. 5 unscheduled UW-F14 Deferred coverage work: Tier-3 LLM eval suite (needs a budget decision), MSW adoption, fakeredis plus a genai seam 5 decision UW-F15 Traceability matrix: extend staging past smoke to GJ2/GJ3/GJ5 (named "the single highest-value gap"), promote GJ1/GJ4 in prod to full journeys, alert on every scheduled run, close the K5 and K8/A16 shipped-but-untested rows, and normalize the 2026-07-17 addendum rows 5 unscheduled UW-F16 A16 cover generation is ❌ across all four test tiers 5 unscheduled UW-F17 Execute r1-live-e2e-checklist.md. The step count is 38, not the 39 this row claimed. Partially executed 2026-08-04 against production at revision f1b561b6 (v0.63.0), recorded in that document's sign-off table: Section 0 ran, 5 of its 7 steps pass with evidence (TLS and cert validity, Supabase build args proven present in the served supabaseClient chunk, Redis plus the RQ worker healthy and polling rq:queue:generation, migrations an exact 49-to-49 set match against the live project, and a same-day local pg_dump). The pass also produced three findings that outlive it: the health-probe step was a false pass and is unreachable through the ingress (UW-L04); the Accounts section's role model was wrong, since is_admin is orthogonal to role and no production account has role='admin', which also undermines Section 1a's landing-surface assertion; and Section 6's cross-family check has no usable third family to test against. That last point was originally written as "production holds only the real family and the isolated e2e test family", which is wrong and is corrected here: production holds three family rows, but the third (0ca7a109) has no user rows at all, so it cannot be signed into and cannot serve as a cross-family subject, and its existence is itself a finding (UW-L05). The check is still meaningful without it, because the test account lives in its own family and the real family holds data the test account must not see. Open prerequisites, all owner-gated: interactive credentials for subs c1f33430 and 21985c35 (31 of the 33 remaining steps need a real sign-in); explicit authorization to spend OpenRouter and classifier quota and write real content into the live family (Sections 2 and 4); a maintenance window for the one mutating Section 0 step (worker restart); and a second device plus a real offline transition (Section 5). The automatable remainder was closed this way on 2026-08-04 rather than by growing the manual list: three new specs in frontend/e2e-prod/ (health-probe, guardian-profiles, guardian-books-and-isolation) now assert, unattended on the existing daily cron, the read-only parts of Sections 1, 3 and 6 plus the server-side leg of Section 5's resume, and the probe that Section 0 got wrong. Every emptiness or count assertion carries a positive control (a rendered heading or the component's own empty-state copy) so an unloaded page cannot pass as a satisfied one, and the redaction check carries a collector-captured-something assertion for the same reason. What stays manual is what automation cannot honestly cover: anything mutating (profile edit/delete, assign/unassign, remove a book), the self-signup and awaiting-approval interstitials the fixed test account can never reach, the real airplane-mode transition and the second physical device in Section 5, and the Section 2/4 steps that spend live LLM and classifier quota. Two consequences worth stating: the new specs assert the POST-fix production state, so the daily cron stays red until homelab-infra redeploys both images, and assertions that depend on live moderation content are deliberately conditional, which means a broken redacted-projection render would be caught only by the response-body scan if every candidate story happened to be clean. Advanced 2026-08-08 against revision 631c0d8a (v0.68.0), now 10 of 38 steps, recorded in that document's sign-off table. Five further steps closed with no interactive session and no production mutation, all from the daily e2e-prod cron plus read-only queries: the health probe (the redeploy it was blocked on has landed, so UW-L04 is confirmed live by three consecutive green runs rather than by merge state), the unauthenticated-redirect and guardian-sign-in steps, and both Section 1a steps. Section 1a's open question is resolved, and the answer was that this checklist was wrong rather than the product: LoginPage.tsx branches on the base role alone, so a dual-role adult correctly lands on /guardian, and the old "not the guardian console" assertion was unsatisfiable by any production account. The pass also found a live P1: UW-L07 / #639, guardian profile resolution reading a Tier 1 table before the RLS context is applied, which empties profile_ids for every guardian in production. That defect now blocks more of this row than the owner gates do: it fails two e2e-prod assertions, and because the failing test sits in a serial describe block, it also prevents the automated read-only halves of Section 1's remaining steps from executing at all. The owner-gated prerequisites listed above are otherwise unchanged. M4.1 blocked UW-F18 15 of 17 naive-user Track B scenarios never run; only K1 and K2 are logged, both blocked by #196. Track B to A promotion never exercised. 5 blocked UW-F19 Weak skips that pass on a construction failure: tests/unit/test_gate.py:469,496 and test_notifications_registry.py:262. Corpus-availability skips silently pass when the catalog is thin. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-F20 0 of 21 skeletons proven end-to-end per skeleton-corpus-story-generation-test-plan.md, plus 3 open decisions (coverage depth, triage owner, tracking location) 5 unscheduled UW-F21 Three continue-on-error: true steps in ci.yml (lines 268, 421, 649); supabase-ci.yml and ci.yml:731 both defer promotion to ci-gate CI hygiene unscheduled UW-F22 Six symbols with no reader anywhere in the codebase, confirmed by the 2026-07-31 vulture calibration. Vulture is right that all six are unreferenced; the consequence differs per symbol, so each needs its own call between wire-it-up and delete-it. (a) flywheel/strategy.py:81 OPEN_PR_PER_CELL = 1 is documented as the per-cell open-PR cap, but cadence.py:194 implements the bound as if cell in open_pr_cells, a set-membership test that hardcodes "at most 1". Behaviour matches the constant TODAY, so nothing is broken; changing the constant would silently do nothing. Latent trap, not a live defect. (b) flywheel/strategy.py:105 TEMPLATE_SET_VERSION = 1 has zero references, and ledger.py's AttemptRecord (lines 105-158) carries no version field, so the ledger genuinely does not record the template-set version its own comment says it should. © core/token_audience.py:42 TokenAudience.GUARDIAN_OIDC = "authenticated" is documentation of Settings.oidc_audience's default rather than dead code, but config.py:592 repeats the literal "authenticated" instead of referencing the member, so two copies of one value can drift with nothing asserting they agree. Fix is default=TokenAudience.GUARDIAN_OIDC.value. (d) generation/authoring_metadata.py:44 SkeletonAuthoringMetadata is a TypedDict referenced only from a docstring cross-reference at import_story.py:235, never used as an annotation. (e) scripts/check_quality_gate.py:85 get_measures is a dead method; the script is invoked by no nox session, workflow, or hook. (f) story_requests/service.py:149 profile_monthly_spend is a public wrapper with no caller; its siblings family_monthly_spend and profile_monthly_spend_by_family both have callers, and the ADR-015 G3 envelope it wraps IS enforced at can_auto_approve (service.py:343-346) via the private _approved_count_since. Dead wrapper only, no control gap. Closed 2026-07-31 on branch fix/uw-f22-unreferenced-symbols, one commit per symbol. (a) Constant deleted and its explanatory comment moved onto the cell in open_pr_cells membership test in cadence.py::_blocking_bound; the flywheel design does not want a tunable here, so the constant was the trap and not the bound (ca105f78). (b) Owner ruled retrofit: AttemptRecord gained a required template_set_version field, to_json/_coerce_record carry it, and rows written before the field read back as a frozen _UNVERSIONED_TEMPLATE_SET = 1 (a historical fact, deliberately not an import of the live constant). No ledger migration was needed; _coerce_record already ignores unknown keys and defaults missing ones (ca105f78). © config.py now uses default=TokenAudience.GUARDIAN_OIDC.value; the member stays out of the distinctness validator by design (issue #251) (6ca818d9). (d) The brief's characterization understated this one. Applying the TypedDict as the annotation on the writer immediately proved it had DRIFTED from the dict it claimed to describe: the four A6/A7 differentiation keys were written by the producer but never added to the shape, and four scalars declared str are in fact written str \| None. The shape was widened to match the producer, and the divergence is recorded in the class docstring (83b4c58a). (e) Owner ruled delete, and the whole script went rather than just the dead method: nothing invoked it, and the org reusable python-sonarcloud.yml already enforces the same gate. Its Ruff per-file-ignore and two doc references went with it (20dba651). (f) can_auto_approve now calls profile_monthly_spend and family_monthly_spend instead of reaching past them to _approved_count_since. The brief's characterization held exactly: dead wrapper, no control gap. The resolved now is threaded into both calls, and test_can_auto_approve_uses_one_instant_for_both_spend_counts fails if either is dropped. Four stale #VERIFY pointers in the same module, all naming a TestBudget class that does not exist, were repaired in the same commit (2755ae26); an earlier draft of this row said five. Every hash cited above was re-pointed after the branch was rebased onto main (post-#518 squash-merge), which rewrote all eight; the pre-rebase hashes resolve only on backup/uw-f22-prerebase. Cite subjects rather than hashes in future rows, since a squash-merge will retire these too. 5 done UW-F23 Generate the vulture --make-whitelist baseline, but only AFTER UW-F22 is closed, otherwise the baseline freezes the six true positives as accepted. Regenerate at commit time: whitelist entries are line-anchored and drift on any edit above them. Residual finding count after the 2026-07-31 calibration is 77 (from 346 raw), all adjudicated false-positive or test-only. Closed 2026-07-31 by vulture_whitelist.py, added on branch fix/uw-f22-unreferenced-symbols in the commit immediately after 9045e52f (a self-citing hash is not available: the row is part of the commit it would name). Final count is 72 entries, not the 71 the closure order implied, and the arithmetic is 77 - 7 + 2. Only 71 of those 72 are adjudicated false positives: forwarded_allow_ips is a deferred TRUE positive, suppressed solely to keep the baseline at exit 0 and tagged inline in vulture_whitelist.py so the deferral stays greppable. It remains scheduled as UW-F25, and the ordering rule at the top of this row is therefore satisfied by the register rather than by the baseline. Two further corrections fall out of the count. First, the 77 was NOT all false-positive or test-only: it also held config.py's rate_limit_redis_cooldown_seconds, the issue #516 symptom, so seven true positives cleared rather than six. Second, widening SkeletonAuthoringMetadata to match its producer (UW-F22 (d)) ADDED two findings, differentiation_level and variation_axis, because those TypedDict keys are written through the *_KEY constants and so the identifiers themselves appear nowhere else; the sibling keys escape only because other code happens to reuse their names as local variables. Both are structural false positives of the same kind the baseline exists to absorb. The baseline is wired in through paths in [tool.vulture], since a whitelist that is not scanned does nothing, and vulture_whitelist.py is excluded from Ruff and BasedPyright because its undefined bare names are the mechanism. uv run vulture now exits 0, so the next finding is a signal. One trap the wiring creates, recorded in the file's own docstring: regeneration must pass src/ scripts/ positionally (uv run vulture src/ scripts/ --make-whitelist), because plain --make-whitelist scans the whitelist alongside the source, finds nothing left to report, and writes an EMPTY file that silently un-suppresses all 72 entries. Hit once while writing this row. CI hygiene done UW-F24 setup_logging() is never called by the served application, so three settings that exist, are documented, and have tests are inert in production. Found 2026-07-31 by the issue #516 generalisation sweep (an AST scan for every attribute read of settings across src/ and scripts/, after a naive name grep produced a false all-clear). Verified: structlog.is_configured() returns False after create_app(), and the only caller anywhere is scripts/backfill_covers_r2.py, a one-off backfill that passes hardcoded arguments rather than settings. Neither RQ worker entrypoint calls it either. Consequences: Settings.log_level, json_logs, and include_timestamp change nothing at runtime; the deployed service renders through structlog's default ConsoleRenderer rather than the JSON handler json_logs=True selects; and add_correlation_id is never installed as a processor, so log lines carry no correlation_id key even though CorrelationMiddleware populates the contextvar and CLAUDE.md's "Example JSON Log Output" shows one. Explicit get_correlation_id() reads still work; only the automatic injection into every log line is missing. Fix is to call setup_logging() from create_app() and both worker entrypoints with the settings values, which will change the log format that container stdout consumers see, so it is a deployment-visible change and not a pure code fix. 5 unscheduled UW-F25 Settings.forwarded_allow_ips is never read in Python. Found by the same 2026-07-31 sweep. The value that actually takes effect is uvicorn's --forwarded-allow-ips CLI flag: hardcoded to 172.16.0.0/12 in the Dockerfile CMD and overridden per stack in docker-compose.yml (${FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS:-172.26.0.0/16}) and docker-compose.prod.yml. Setting CYO_ADVENTURE_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS in an environment therefore does nothing, while the field's docstring reads as though it governs the behaviour. Security-adjacent: this is the list of proxies trusted to set X-Forwarded-*, so the resolution is either to have the entrypoint derive the flag from the setting (one source of truth) or to delete the field and repoint its rationale at the Dockerfile and compose files. Do not simply drop it without recording where the real value lives; the docstring is currently the only prose explanation of the choice. Note that vulture no longer reports this: the UW-F23 baseline suppresses it (tagged UW-F25 inline in vulture_whitelist.py), so this row is now the only signal keeping it visible. Delete that whitelist entry as part of the fix. 5 unscheduled UW-F26 .github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml's trigger block (the on: stanza around lines 13-23) fires only on push to main/develop and on workflow_dispatch; it carries no pull_request trigger and no merge_group trigger. Consequence: no pull request ever receives SonarCloud analysis, and the gap reads as success rather than absence: querying Sonar for a PR's issues returns an empty list, and the PR quality-gate endpoint 404s, so both signals look "clean" when they actually mean "no analysis ran," letting a reviewer certify a PR against a signal that does not exist. The trigger set is not an oversight; the workflow already carries a comment block explaining a prior attempt at no-build: true on pull_request failed every run with error: Distribution cyo-adventure==... @ editable+. can't be installed because it is marked as --no-build but has no binary distribution, so someone has already been in this file. Flagged in review of PR #619, and again in review of PR #621 on 2026-08-05; no open GitHub issue and no other row in this register cites it. Left unscheduled rather than fixed inline, and the in-repo comment names the real blocker rather than the obvious one: no known input on the org reusable workflow (ByronWilliamsCPA/.github/python-sonarcloud.yml, not readable from this repo) installs dependencies without also running the full coverage-generating test suite, and fail-on-quality-gate is already forced off outside push, so a PR-time run was advisory with no way to act on its result. The workflow's own #VERIFY marker sets the next step: read python-sonarcloud.yml for a skip-tests-but-still-install input before trying no-build again. The actionable residual is therefore review hygiene rather than a missing gate: a reviewer must not read an empty PR issue queue or a 404 quality gate as a clean result, which is exactly the mistake #621's review had to guard against. Confirmed 2026-08-13, still BLOCKED on the prerequisite this row's own workflow comment names. The #VERIFY in sonarcloud.yml says to add the org's .github repo to a session and check python-sonarcloud.yml for a skip-tests-but-still-install input before retrying no-build. That was attempted here and add_repo for ByronWilliamsCPA/.github requires an approval this non-interactive session cannot obtain, so the reusable workflow's inputs remain unreadable and no correct pull_request path can be designed. Deliberately NOT worked around by adding a pull_request trigger blind: the documented failure mode is that every PR run errors at the editable install, which would trade "no signal" for "a permanently red workflow", and fail-on-quality-gate is already forced off outside push so a PR run would be advisory either way.
