Found 2026-08-16 reviewing #724. useFlowedStop states that outside a resume "the predecessor is a real branch (or there is no predecessor) so the prefix is empty and this is exactly composeStop". That holds for three of the four terminal reasons and fails for loop, whose terminal has exactly ONE visible choice and is therefore tappable. Traced against the shared corpus fixture schema/conformance/stop_traces.json::loop_back_ends_stop (s_stop_loop, band 10-13, so a flowed band; n_q's only choice targets n_p): after the fresh stop [n_p, n_q] closes on the loop guard, tapping c_to_p gives path=[n_p, n_q, n_p], flowedPrefix returns ['n_q'], and the composed stop becomes nodeIds=['n_q','n_p'] with the engine left at n_p. Three visible consequences: the prose renders n_q (which the child just read) ahead of n_p; startIndex resolves to the last index so NO CHOOSE is sent and n_q's on_enter never re-fires, which is exactly the counter a loop_and_grow story exists to grow; and choiceState becomes n_p, so the child is offered the other room's choice. Before this change the same tap produced [n_p, n_q] with the engine at n_q. Not reachable in publishable content, and that is the whole finding. A closed single-choice cycle is an SCC with no exit edge, which validator/layer1.py::_check_trap_loops rejects as L1-5; confirmed empirically, the only flowed-band fixture with this shape is tests/fixtures/storybook/invalid/graph/trap_loop.json, and every loop_and_grow skeleton in the catalog sits at 3-5 or 5-8, both non-flowed. So no child can hit it today. But flowedPrefix's docstring promises that any ambiguity "stops the walk and yields the shorter prefix, so the worst case is today's behavior rather than a wrong one", and here the worst case is a wrong one: the guarantee is being carried by a validator rule the reader neither references nor can see. Why it is not fixed here: the obvious gates each break a legitimate case. Gating reconstruction on tracked === null (resume only) breaks Go back, which lands on the previous stop's terminal and genuinely needs the prefix. Refusing any prefix that closes a cycle also breaks the resumed-cycle case stops.test.ts already pins ('ends a resumed cycle where it originally ended'), because the two are indistinguishable from flowedPrefix's inputs alone: both see a single-choice predecessor and a path that revisits. The discriminator has to come from the caller, which knows whether the engine moved forward (a tap) or backward (Go back) or not at all (a mount), most likely by comparing reading.path.length against the tracked stop's. That is a reader-semantics decision under ADR-026, so it wants an owner call and a test for each of the three entries rather than a guess. 4b unscheduled UW-F44 modal.py cannot recognise a token-budget exhaustion, so it retries one deterministically. ModalProvider._extract_completion guards empty content correctly (if not content: catches both None and "") but raises it as leg_fatal=False, and it never digs finish_reason. run_with_retries therefore reissues the identical request at the identical max_tokens with exponential backoff before failing as exhausted, burning the whole retry budget on calls that cannot succeed. openrouter.py already implements the correct treatment (leg_fatal=finish_reason == "length", with the cause worded into the error); port it. Second item in the same change: dig_reasoning_tokens reads only OpenRouter's nested usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens and modal.py never calls it, so the Modal leg collects no reasoning telemetry at all and budget sizing cannot be driven from measurements. Measured and evidenced in handoff-modal-deepseek-v4-smoke-test-2026-08-20.md. Experimental-only per ADR-010, so this gates real Modal use rather than production today. 5 unscheduled UW-F45 The reader suite's shared SyncApi double accepts every revision, so no unit test there can see an optimistic-concurrency defect. Found 2026-08-24 while closing UW-F39 and UW-F40, which were both revision-stamping races. ReaderPage.test.tsx's okApi() returns {status: 200} for every putReadingState whatever state_revision the body carries, and it backs most of that file's ~50 tests. The real PUT /v1/reading-state rejects a mismatched revision with a 409, so an entire class of defect (two writers stamping the same base) was structurally invisible to the unit tier and only ever surfaced in e2e-real, where it presented as three unrelated-looking failures across three specs. #761 adds one concurrency-enforcing double alongside okApi() rather than replacing it, because most tests there are not about revisions and the permissive double keeps them readable. The work here is the sweep that commit deliberately did not do: audit the other reader and offline doubles (src/offline/sync.test.ts, ReaderRoute.test.tsx, AuthContext.test.tsx) for the same shape, and decide which of them should enforce the precondition their real endpoint enforces. General principle worth carrying past this row: a test double that silently accepts a precondition the real dependency enforces converts a whole defect class into a green suite. 5 unscheduled UW-F46 Nothing detects that the scheduled-failure alerting itself has stopped working, and its failure mode is silence. Fourteen schedule-only workflows now delegate their only notification channel to one composite action (.github/actions/ci-failure-issue), which is a real improvement on eleven drifted copies: the fleet-wide invariants are executable now (tests/unit/test_ci_failure_action_contract.py) and the script's behaviour runs against Octokit doubles on every push (.github/actions/ci-failure-issue/test/reconcile.test.mjs, the alert-action leg of ci-gate). It also concentrates the risk: a defect that survives both, or a GITHUB_TOKEN whose issues: write scope is revoked by an org policy change, silences all fourteen at once, and no signal distinguishes that from a fortnight with nothing wrong. Issue #667 is the measured cost of this shape at one-workflow scale: sixteen consecutive nightly backups cancelled at the concurrency gate, zero jobs dispatched, no failure reported, and seventeen days before anyone noticed. Two of the three legs that gap is now closed on are new in #771; the third, liveness, is not, and cannot be tested from inside the thing being monitored. Proposed: a heartbeat that asserts the mechanism ran rather than that it reported nothing. Cheapest credible version is a weekly workflow that files and immediately resolves a [canary] issue through the same action and fails if either leg does not land, which exercises the token scope, the assignment path, and the lookup against the real API. That is a canary, not a monitor: it proves the action works on the day it runs, and does not prove any particular workflow's cron is alive. Whether per-workflow cron liveness is worth a second mechanism (a dead-man's-switch per marker) is an owner call and explicitly out of scope here. Deferred from #771's review as too large for that PR and requiring a decision it should not make unilaterally. 5 unscheduled UW-F47 A #VERIFY marker inside .github/ is invisible to the RAD citation gate, so it can name a test that no longer exists and nothing fails. scripts/check_rad_citations.py "only ever parses .py, .ts and .tsx" by its own docstring, and the check-rad-citations hook's files: pattern admits only four things (Python under src/, Python under scripts/, .ts/.tsx under frontend/src/, and the baseline TOML), so it excludes .github/ entirely. That was harmless while no marker lived there. #771 put the first load-bearing ones in .github/actions/ci-failure-issue/action.yml: its #EDGE concurrency marker cites tests/unit/test_ci_failure_action_contract.py for two invariants (no call site in a multi-leg matrix job, every call site's workflow carries a concurrency: group) precisely so they stop being prose, and its #CRITICAL external resources marker points at the assignee-drop assertions. Those citations resolve today, verified by hand at merge. The gap is that renaming or deleting either test leaves a marker asserting a guarantee nobody checks, which is worse than an uncited assumption because it reads as verified. Proposed: extend the checker to parse # comments in .github/**/*.yml (YAML shares Python's comment character, so the marker grammar already applies) and widen the hook's files: pattern to match, then re-baseline. Scope note: the hook's own comment already records the same blindness for supabase/ and frontend/e2e/, so the fix should widen the gate once for all three trees rather than special-casing .github/. Surfaced while reviewing #771. 5 unscheduled

docs.title: Cluster G: content diversity and catalog workstream
docs.text:
roadmap.md and PROJECT-PLAN.md both state outright that this workstream has no line item anywhere. This cluster is that line item. Live specs are story-diversity-plan-v2.md, story-diversity-implementation-plan.md, and story-diversity-review-errata.md; the remediation plan, execution plan, and original analysis are superseded and must not be tracked from.

Phase label G in this register means the "Content workstream: diversity and catalog growth" section of roadmap.md, created 2026-07-28 to give this work its first phase home.

ID Item Source Phase Status UW-G01 A20: 14 of 16 skeletons and 4,305 <<FILL>> nodes unslotted; needs a family-based plan generator first. Largest single item in the workstream. Canonical with UW-A29. plan-v2, s4 handoff content unscheduled UW-G02 OQ-4: 11 stateful Tier-2 skeletons unmigrated, plus the series-level binding design ws2 content unscheduled UW-G03 A9 item 2: restructure the-sunken-temple (5 variables, 20 conditions, 75 effects, plus a 35-ending remix to 0.0710) s4 handoff content unscheduled UW-G04 Per-band ATG calibration: _BAND_THRESHOLDS is still {}, so the anti-template guard stays advisory ws0, ws1 content unscheduled UW-G05 WS-0 Phase 3 judge-model calibration run; sentence-shape correlation as a gating signal; persisted theme signatures on StorybookVersion; leaf-cluster ECS partition ws0 content unscheduled UW-G06 ECS and RAR dashboard surfacing; served-window ECS DB loader; young-band panel growth; same-theme cross-tree pairs; weekly non-required judge workflow ws0 phase2 content unscheduled UW-G07 Series and carries_state partner exclusion; ATG wiring into api/node_edit.py re-screen; threading briefs into ATG ws1 content unscheduled UW-G08 Grammar-based composer (§7, explicitly deferred); §5.5 deferred-within-M5 items (tier promotion, variable add/remove, stateful grafts, restart-on-fail rewiring); OQ-8 PL-23 rule family ws5 content unscheduled UW-G09 WS-6 fresh-generated trees as the flywheel feed; lift the lineage-depth cap (OQ-5); in-app promotion-review surface; flywheel-reports/ cycle reports ws8 content unscheduled UW-G10 Binding cache (OQ-3); story-skeletons.md contract column ws2 content unscheduled UW-G11 A10 teen short-cell zero candidates returning 422; A15 retire-for-quality; A17 tombstone card plan-v2 content unscheduled UW-G12 Eight items behind prerequisites: reading telemetry, PL-25 fail-depth floor, outcome-mix floor, challenge mode and permadeath, alternate beat phrasings, per-profile_id ATG scoping, guardian visibility ceiling, growing small cells. Open prerequisite: SQ-11's alternate-beats ADR (story-structure-improvement-plan.md §1.1, the value-critical chain), which unblocks the alternate-beat-phrasings item; the rest follow their own named prerequisites. Phase moved post-launch to content on 2026-08-06 by owner ruling OG7: this row lands in the Content workstream once unblocked, and blocked already carries the not-yet-schedulable meaning, so post-launch was asserting deferral twice and contradicting the plan that schedules SQ-11 first plan-v2 §5 content blocked UW-G13 Wave 5: 36 new skeletons, 2 per production cell; the dagger-cell 460-node ceiling experiment; the Tier-2 stateful pilot story-inventory content unscheduled UW-G14 23 filled stories committed to main are unpublished; 3 legacy-shaped fills need normalization at import. Mechanism corrected 2026-08-03: issue #347 records a production import run on 2026-07-21 landing 25 stories at in_review, so the open step is the separate admin promotion to visibility='catalog' (publishing/catalog_publish.py::promote_catalog_story), not the import. Live database state is unverified; checking it is step 1 of the SQ-01 runbook. Phase moved content to R1 on 2026-08-06 by owner ruling OG7 (story-structure-improvement-plan.md §8.1): a library with zero reachable catalog books is the core reading loop failing, not a catalog-growth shortfall, so this is an R1 usability gap rather than ordinary Content-workstream cadence. It also blocks the M5.1 sign-off, whose exit definition is every family-tier register row at delivered status; that is stated here rather than in Phase because the register permits one token per cell. Owner ruling OG1 (same date) sets the terms: promote everything passing the #529 sweep, kid bands first, holding back the-sunken-temple and the-harrowstone-keep pending the A9 restructure, and treating all three inherited issue #347 questions (billing-defect fix confirmed, hard-block vs advisory settled, per-stage fail_safe direction audited) as blocking prerequisites of the runbook. Re-counted 2026-08-25 against production: 17 books sit at in_review and 10 are published to visibility='catalog', unchanged since the 2026-07-21 import (the newest storybook_version row in production is dated 2026-07-28). Promotion is gated behind the review gate, and at least 12 of the 17 cannot honestly clear it: their stored reports carry no real verdicts at all. Two of the remaining five carry hidden fail-safe PASSes on a large share of their nodes (24 of 148, 22 of 25), so the honest count is 12 or 14 depending on a threshold the census logs as an open owner decision (section 7.2), not on further measurement. See UW-C364 and the 2026-08-25 census. This row therefore depends on the Stage D sweep, not merely on an admin finding time to promote. draft-stories-manifest R1 unscheduled UW-G15 F1 --series-id on import; F2 auto-repair silently replaces imported content; F3 carried variables invert acquisition branches. Restated in the ceiling-scale review; track via AL-*. series-stress-test content unscheduled UW-G16 Story-quality residuals A, B, C (skeleton promotion gate, RL-13 noise, rule-catalog drift); B and C are product decisions story-quality-lessons content decision UW-G17 Five research reconciliation actions (exposure ratio, per-band fail-state, reconvergence targets, an independent FK/Lexile gate, edition-family anchoring) plus four open calibration conflicts. Needs an ADR-011 amendment. research post-launch decision UW-G18 SR-8 is reserved and claimed by PR #416; L2-8 emits no ID; validator-rules.md contradicts itself on whether SR-8 is implemented validator-rules doc unscheduled UW-G19 Generation cost and latency instrumentation, as a prerequisite to any architecture comparison. Correction 2026-08-23: the premise below was true when written and is now false, and the row's own text was the thing that had gone stale. The money half shipped on 2026-08-11 (migration 20260811160000_add_generation_job_provider_accounting.sql): generation_job now carries input_tokens, output_tokens, provider_call_count, provider_unknown_calls, provider_duration_ms, cost_usd and cost_complete, written by generation/worker.py::_stamp_provider_accounting off a per-job UsageLedger, priced through core/pricing.py, with cost_complete marking a lower bound rather than letting an unpriced call read as free. Cost claims about a generation run are therefore measurements now, subject to that flag. The original premise text follows for provenance: "the generation job record carries status, model, provider, prompt version and report, and carries no token counts, no cost and no duration, so every cost claim we could make today is an estimate presented as a measurement." Residual, which is what keeps this row open: job wall-clock duration as distinct from provider_duration_ms (which the column's own docstring says is not the job's runtime), retry count, repair count, and validator-failure count. Human review minutes came off this list on 2026-08-23, one day after the correction above was written: #746 added the submitted pipeline event and publishing/gate_metrics.py, which pairs gate entry with released/sent_back and reports median_duration_seconds, send_back_rate and mean_rounds_to_release. That measurement is PROSPECTIVE only, by design: a decision with no preceding entry is dropped rather than paired with a neighbour, and every pre-migration released row is such a row, so there is no historical review-minutes baseline and D3's notional rate is what the model has to use until observations accumulate. The derived-measures page is step 4's R-5, not this row. Record per run, split by what is already recorded so the list stops reading as wholly outstanding: input and output tokens, cost and final status are columns on generation_job today; human review minutes is measured prospectively by the submitted gate entry described above and is no longer sought here; wall-clock duration, retry count, repair count and validator failures are the residual this row stays open for. Derived measures: cost per candidate, per validator-passing candidate, per approved book, cost of failed books, repair as a percentage of generation, review minutes per approved book, and cost by band and graph size. This is generation operations telemetry and contains no child content, so it sits outside the S10 boundary entirely. Raised by the third external review, which correctly refuses to rank the candidate architectures without it. external-review-3 content unscheduled UW-G20 Privacy-minimized all-pairs novelty ledger. The owner has ruled there is no recency window: a child may read any two books in their library back to back, so novelty must hold pairwise across the whole library rather than against recent history. Persist only what a novelty screen needs (pseudonymous profile, book version, experienced node ids, mechanic, device and solution-rule identifiers, ending, first and last seen day) and explicitly not fine-grained timestamps, hesitation, latency, guardian-facing choice-by-choice replay, or story prose. Keep the per-request cost sublinear with inverted indexes over device, solution rule, premise family, cognitive operation and mechanic-sequence hash rather than pairwise evaluation. Depends on the retention and purge design already specified in reader-path-engagement-design.md, whose route data currently arrives and is discarded. external-review-3 content unscheduled UW-G21 Replace the single similarity score with an auditable feature vector. Report exact device collisions, exact solution collisions, repeated mechanic count, longest repeated operation sequence, premise-family overlap, world overlap, cast overlap, topology similarity and shared free text as separate values, and do not collapse them into one weighted number until there is evidence the weighting tracks a product outcome. Follows 16o's own warning about invented weights, and the owner's ruling that the world, cast and topology exclusions are not permanent: those three become measured and reported rather than excluded in the prompt. external-review-3 content unscheduled UW-G22 Re-run skeleton-free generation with every omitted constraint supplied, then at scale. The 6-of-6 structural-validity result failed only on rules never given to the model (branch-depth budget, opening-decision floor, ending schema). Supply the complete machine-readable contract, generate once, run the external validator, return concise counterexamples for repair, and record first-pass validity separately from post-repair validity. Then two graphs near 100 nodes, since the one production-scale run halted at the guards with badly degraded reading level. Do not add a self-review prompt; the model must not certify its own output. Now the leading production candidate per the third external review, given the owner's ruling that the team may launch all new. external-review-3 content unscheduled UW-G23 Disambiguate binding contracts from narrative contracts in the catalog. 47 skeletons carry a *.contract.json, which is a binding contract (slots, lexicon, default binding); 2 carry a *.narrative.json, which is the narrative contract every proposed architecture depends on. An external reviewer read "2 of 61 have contracts" as "the other 59 are bare topology", which is wrong in both directions: 47 have a binding layer, and all 84 carry sparse formal structure (recounted 2026-08-22: conditions on 0.9 percent and effects on 1.5 percent of 22,165 choices, on_enter effects on 0.4 percent of 15,470 nodes; the absolute counts barely moved, so the percentages fell only because the catalog grew). Rename so the two cannot be confused, and state the coverage of each wherever the bottleneck is cited. external-review-3 content unscheduled UW-G24 Regenerate the catalog counts quoted across the planning docs, and give them a source of truth. The figures "61 graphs", "11,458 nodes" and "3-4 skeletons per cell" were correct on 2026-08-12 and were then copied forward by hand into later documents without re-running; at 2026-08-22 the catalog is 84 shells and 15,470 nodes, with 81 shells declaring metadata.production_eligible: true, of which 74 are reachable in an offered cell and together cover all 18 cells ADR-011 offers (validator/band_profile.py::_PRODUCTION_CELLS) at 3 to 5 per cell (median 4). The 24-cell band-by-length-by-style cross-product is not the offered grid, so coverage must not be reported against it; the six combinations it adds are ones ADR-011 does not sell. The 2026-08-22 research brief is corrected; a sweep of origin/main on 2026-08-22 for the stale phrasings (61 skeletons/61 graphs, 11,458, 3-4 skeletons per cell, N of 61) found roughly 40 further sites, so the remaining work is a classification pass, not a find-and-replace. Sites split three ways. Asserts current state, so correct it: roadmap.md (line 236), story-diversity-plan-v2.md, diversity-test-register.md (the Q-1 and Q-2 rows), cyo-framework-problem-and-structures-2026-08-10.md, UW-A29, UW-C114, UW-C156 and UW-G23 above, and src/cyo_adventure/storybook/field_minors.py (line 6). Records a dated measurement, so date it rather than rewriting it: the ADR-011/ADR-023/ADR-025/ADR-026 measurement passages, the dated review and handoff documents (cyo-review-response-2026-08-11.md, the 2026-08-09 schema review, the kid-appeal review, the measurement workplan), the AL rows in authoring-lessons-log.md, and scripts/check_promotion_bundle.py (line 294) and src/cyo_adventure/generation/skeleton.py (line 83), both of which already self-date. Needs a judgement call: three test docstrings that quote a catalog count while the test itself iterates the live catalog, so the prose and the population have silently diverged (tests/unit/test_policy.py:1910, tests/unit/test_analyze_sibling_exposure.py:814, tests/unit/test_orchestrator.py:985), plus scripts/check_skeleton.py:92 ("40 of 61 skeletons"), whose advisory-incidence claim was never re-measured against the 84-shell catalog. Hand-copied counts will go stale again, so the work is a small script that emits the census (shells, nodes, commissioned words, per-band and per-cell eligibility) plus a decision on where each doc cites it from; scripts/flywheel_report.py::_cells_by_key already groups production-eligible entries by exact cell and is the natural extension point. Also re-derive the Q-1 cell-exhaustion arithmetic, whose conclusion was computed on the superseded per-cell figure. This row was originally scoped to editing prose and recorded that no authoring-lessons row was owed. That ceased to be true once the row's own work became a tooling change made in service of authoring, which is on the CLAUDE.md trigger list: see AL-556 to AL-560. Progress, 2026-08-22: the census script and its generated doc (catalog-census.md) ship in PR #740, and the "asserts current state" bucket is cleared: roadmap.md, diversity-test-register.md (including the re-derived Q-1 arithmetic), UW-A29, UW-C114, UW-C156 and UW-G23 above, and storybook/field_minors.py (which now carries no count at all). Two of that bucket's sites were reclassified to "date it" on reading them: story-diversity-plan-v2.md section 1 and cyo-framework-problem-and-structures-2026-08-10.md are measurement bases whose rows record what a named procedure returned on a date, so each now carries a dated recount banner naming the values that moved rather than edited figures that were never re-run. Progress, 2026-08-23 (PR #740 review): a site none of the three buckets listed, docs/architecture/story-skeletons.md ("Of the 21 catalogued skeletons", two lines below its own generated 84-row table), now cites the census instead of quoting counts; the sweep that could not have found it is UW-C340/AL-558. The census itself was also conflating two quantities under one "production-eligible shells" label (81 shells declare the flag, 74 are reachable in an offered cell) and now reports both separately (AL-557). Progress, 2026-08-23 (date-it bucket and judgement calls closed): every site in the "date it" bucket now either carries its measurement date or cites the census, and none of its figures were rewritten. Dated banners: ADR-011 (under the 2026-07-27 clarification, which the earlier "54 of 61" site already defers to), ADR-023 (over the verification-notes section), the 2026-08-09 schema review, the kid-appeal review, the measurement workplan, the 2026-08-10 research brief, cyo-review-response-2026-08-11.md, the 2026-08-15 measurement handoff, the 2026-08-21 sourcing test plan, the 2026-07-26 S4 handoff, the 2026-08-09 skeleton-free proposal, story-structure-diversity-critical-analysis.md, and the persistent-characters spec. Inline dating: ADR-023 section 5, ADR-025 (line 210), ADR-026 (both 0 of 61 sites), PROJECT-PLAN.md, story-diversity-review-errata.md, story-personalization-implementation-plan.md, story-structure-improvement-plan.md, story-structure-implementation-briefs.md, diversity-test-register.md's Q-2 row, and scripts/check_promotion_bundle.py:294 (which said "at the time of writing", not a date). The ~19 AL sites need no per-row edit: authoring-lessons-log.md now states in its preamble that a row's counts are dated by that row's Date. The four judgement calls are closed too. The three test docstrings (tests/unit/test_policy.py, tests/unit/test_analyze_sibling_exposure.py, tests/unit/test_orchestrator.py) now cite the census and carry their measurement dates instead of quoting a count the test itself no longer bounds. scripts/check_skeleton.py:92 was re-measured rather than dated, because its claim is about a gate rather than a catalog: 64 of 84 shells fire a strict-blocking advisory, dominated by grammar (CG-3 64, CG-2 54, CG-1 41, against PL-23 31, PL-24 19, PL-26 6), which corroborates the UW-C116/UW-C158 finding that the strict delta is entirely CG-*. The first attempt at that re-measurement was wrong in a way worth recording: a bare run_gate(doc) returns no CG-* at all (UW-C24), so it reported 35 of 84 and looked like a result. See AL-577. Still open: the decision on where each document cites the census from and whether --check should gate, plus the gate-outcome emitter noted below. Also noted while re-measuring UW-C116: gate outcomes decay exactly like counts and have no emitter. "The strict bar passes 2 of 61" had drifted to 20 of 84 and its "retires 97% of the catalog" cost to 74%, which is a 23-point error in the input to an open decision. The census script covers what the catalog is; nothing covers what a gate would say about it, and that is the natural second emitter. brief-review-2026-08-22 doc unscheduled UW-G25 Schedule the generation-review workstream. The thirteen-agent review of the 2026-08-22 research brief produced 14 critical and high findings, five condensed medium and low bundles, and a seven-step sequence, none of which had a phase home. generation-review-workstream-plan-2026-08-22.md traces every finding to a step with acceptance criteria, and stops at four owner decisions rather than planning past them. Two are now ruled (2026-08-23): D1 provisionally and D3 partially, which together release step 4's structure, step 6's R-8 replication and step 7; D2 and D4 remain open. The four as originally framed: D1 which leg fills (re-opened by PR #738 after the "best prose model" claim proved to be a cost figure), D2 whether the strict bar is the production bar (re-measured 2026-08-22: retires 73% of the 74 shells reachable in an offered cell, not 97%, and the entire delta is the CG-* grammar family with zero structural-only failures), D3 the economics target a per-book cost cap would derive from, and D4 where documents cite the census and whether --check should gate. Steps 1r, 2, 3 and most of 5 were unblocked from the start. Steps 1, 1r and 2 are now complete (PRs #738, #740, #742, #743); step 3's instruments are built but neither measurement has run. brief-review-2026-08-22 doc unscheduled

docs.title: Cluster H: story personalization (ADR-023)
docs.text:
The feature has an ADR, two large planning documents, and a merged Stage A. Neither master document references any of it. This cluster is therefore recorded as blocked, not scheduled: that is its accurate state.

This is what keeps ADR-023 at proposed. 7 decision UW-H04 K19 Route A copy rewrite is a hard precondition on the G18 flag, paired with PR #415's A11. Register-only today. 4b unscheduled UW-H05 R8 they/them handling deferred; ring-3 aggregate rendering; free-text dedications out of scope 4b unscheduled UW-H06 Capability rows G18 and K20 have no phase home, which is why S10 and S11's ADR-023 extensions have none either 4b unscheduled UW-H07 Ring-3 exclusion must land as a test in the S12 work post-launch unscheduled UW-H08 Task R3's open half: storybook_version.sentinel_manifest is written once at persist time and never refreshed when a later in-place blob rewrite changes what the blob carries (moderation/pipeline.py adopting a repair, api/node_edit.py applying an edit). docs.title: Cluster I: reader UX and player
docs.text: ID Item Source Phase Status UW-I01 A11 request-page reshape, gated on a naive-user session with real children that only the owner can run. Note the ID collision with capability-register A11. s5 handoff 4b blocked UW-I02 A13b "Try a different way" three-hop ending-screen rewind; A18 differentiate the two back-chevrons.
