docs.title: Cluster J: remediation-plan and console gaps
docs.text: ID Item Source Phase Status UW-J01 P7 auto-assign-on-publish, blocked on a requested_by_profile_id migration. Raised independently by the persona audit. Unblocked 2026-08-15: the named blocker does not exist and probably has not since before this row was written. The 2026-07-17 remediation plan recorded it as "auto-assign needs a schema migration threading requested_by_profile_id request -> concept -> storybook (no such link exists)", and this row inherited that wording. The link is complete in the shipped schema, under a different column name than the blocker named, which is the likeliest reason nobody re-checked: story_request.profile_id holds the requesting child profile and story_request.resulting_storybook_id holds the storybook the request produced (both db/models.py), and publishing/service.py::approve already calls _stamp_resulting_storybook_id and emits EventType.RELEASED at the exact point an auto-assign hook would run, so both ends are in scope of one function and no migration is required. Re-raised independently by the 2026-08-14 registration walkthrough (onboarding-flow-walkthrough-2026-08-14.md) as its highest-severity finding: api/library.py:425 hard-requires a storybook_assignment row and api/assignments.py:328 is its only writer, so a guardian who requested a story for a named child still lands that child on an empty shelf. Scheduled as Wave 1 item 1a of onboarding-overhaul-plan-2026-08-15.md, which also carries the three constraints the implementation must reuse rather than reimplement (the K13 age-band ceiling in assign_storybook, assignment idempotency, and the BOOK_ASSIGNED event that drives the notification split in UW-J23). Note the remediation plan's own P7 row still carries the stale blocker text; it is left as the historical record and this row is canonical. remediation, persona audit, registration walkthrough 4b unscheduled UW-J23 The story_ready notification claims a shelf the book did not reach. notifications/registry.py:147 composes "It has been approved and published to your family library", which a guardian reads as "it is on the shelf", while the book is assigned to nobody; the correct-sounding sibling composer _compose_book_assigned (line 159) is the one that only fires on a real assignment. Rewrite the published-but-unassigned message to name the remaining step and link to the assign control. Stays worth doing after UW-J01 lands, because auto-assign covers only the single-child request path: catalog books, second children, and profile-less requests still publish unassigned, and a rare wrong message is worse than a common one because nobody is looking for it. Wave 1 item 1b of the onboarding overhaul plan. Scope grew 2026-08-15: PR #720 put the same false promise on the marketing homepage ("Once you approve a book it lands on their shelf right away"). That sentence was corrected on branch claude/minor-guardian-registration-flow-o0cmaf and reworded to stay true after auto-assign ships, so it needs no second pass; the notification copy this row covers is still outstanding. Treat the landing footnote, the story_ready composer, and UW-J26's Books page state as one claim that must agree. registration walkthrough, PR #720 4b unscheduled UW-J24 Does an uninvited self-signup stay behind the admin approval gate? Today it does: api/onboarding.py provisions every uninvited subject at status="awaiting_approval" and require_principal then refuses them everything including GET /v1/me, so a brand-new family waits on a platform admin they have no relationship with and no channel to reach, with nothing notifying either party in either direction. Coherent for an invite-shaped deployment; a dead end for anything resembling public signup, which is how the 2026-08-14 walkthrough hit it. The ruling decides the shape of the work, not merely its timing: keeping the gate makes it a notification and queue problem (UW-J29, UW-J30), while opening it makes it a compensating-controls problem, and the guardian-created invite path must keep its gate either way for the reason api/onboarding.py already documents (a guardian can name any address and would otherwise capture a stranger into their family on that person's first sign-in). Sits next to the still-open VPC method decision (UW-N02, UW-A52) and interacts with UW-J25: opening this gate while KWS verification stays off leaves no adulthood check anywhere in the product. Owner to rule: the project owner. Wave 0 item D1 of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b decision UW-J25 Is kws_verification_required turned on, and does a plain age affirmation ship regardless? The flag defaults to False (core/config.py:1159), so on a default deployment the adulthood-verification step is skipped entirely and the only checks are the self-attestation checkbox on the consent form and the admin gate UW-J24 may remove. The flag flip itself is counsel-gated and already tracked (UW-M03, UW-N02); this row exists to make the combination visible, because the two decisions have never been read together and the unsafe pairing is not obvious from either one alone. The separable half is the age affirmation before the OAuth button (UW-J33), which is not verification, must not be worded as though it were, and needs no counsel ruling. Owners to rule: the project owner with privacy counsel. Wave 0 item D2 of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b decision UW-J26 frontend/src/guardian/BooksPage.tsx lists published books without distinguishing one on a child's shelf from one on nobody's, so the gap UW-J01 and UW-J23 describe is invisible on the one page a guardian would look at to find it. Add the unassigned state and a direct assign affordance from the list. This is the recovery path for any guardian who already hit the gap, including everyone who hit it before auto-assign shipped, which is why it is not made redundant by UW-J01. Wave 1 item 1c of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b unscheduled UW-J27 Nothing holds the request-to-shelf path in place end to end. Needs an e2e-real spec walking request -> publish -> child library that asserts the book is readable with no manual assign step, plus an integration test that a band-exceeding auto-assign is refused while the publish still succeeds (the K13 ceiling must fail the assign, not the publish). Without it UW-J01 is a behavior no test pins, which is the same condition that let the original gap survive a persona audit in July and be re-found by hand in August. Wave 1 item 1d of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b unscheduled UW-J28 Two strings describe a platform admin as though they were family, sending a guardian looking for a person who does not exist: GuardianAwaitingApprovalPage.tsx ("A family administrator needs to approve your account") and ConsolePage.tsx ("Stories are checked by your family's safety reviewer"). Both are wrong under either outcome of UW-J24, so this does not wait on that ruling. Same change adds the existing public /support link to the awaiting-approval screen, which is the one screen in the flow where a stuck guardian currently has nowhere to go and no ETA. Wave 2 item 2a of the onboarding overhaul plan. Widened 2026-08-15, then closed the same day. PR #720 (merged as 5f38917) promoted the same misattribution to the marketing homepage, which grew the row from two console strings to five strings across three files and raised it from a console-copy defect to a claims-accuracy one: the new landing page carried "You approve, then they read" plus "you always have the final word" (an authority a guardian does not hold: api/approval.py requires the admin role on every mutating handler, and api/node_edit.py's docstring states "approval itself stays admin-only regardless"), a trust card titled "A grown-up approves every story", and a footnote promising "Once you approve a book it lands on their shelf right away" (false a second way, see UW-J01: api/library.py requires a storybook_assignment row that publishing never writes). #720's own honesty pass audited claims against ADR-018 and ADR-014 but not against the authorization model, which is why all five survived it. Note the reason these read as true to their authors: on this deployment the single family's adult is dual-role, so "you approve" holds for them and fails for exactly the new families the funnel exists to attract. Closed on branch claude/minor-guardian-registration-flow-o0cmaf: the guardian's two real controls are named instead (passage editing, G6; per-child assignment, G16), the reviewer is named as ours rather than the reader's ("our safety reviewer", the possessive dropped in both the trust card and ConsolePage.tsx), the awaiting-approval copy names who actually acts and stops promising a message nothing sends (that promise is UW-J29), and the /support link this row asked for is on the waiting screen. Pinned by five tests across LandingPage.test.tsx, ConsolePage.test.tsx, and GuardianAwaitingApprovalPage.test.tsx, each asserting the old string's ABSENCE alongside the replacement's presence so deleting the section cannot pass; the two landing assertions were mutation-verified by reintroducing the old copy and confirming they fail. registration walkthrough, PR #720 now done UW-J29 Nothing fires when a self-signup lands and nothing fires when it clears. EventType carries USER_MANAGED but no signup event, and notifications/service.py resolves every recipient through a family, so there is no admin-facing delivery path at all; the awaiting-approval page's own 20-second poll is the only feedback in the entire loop. Needs a signup event, an admin-scoped delivery path for it (the first admin-facing notification, so this is where the family-scoping assumption gets its first real test), and a guardian-facing notification on approval. Blocked on UW-J24: if that ruling opens the gate, most of this work does not need doing. Wave 2 item 2b of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b blocked UW-J30 admin/UserManagementPage.tsx's Users tab lists users with no status filter and no pending-accounts view, so approving a self-signup requires knowing to go looking for one. Add the filtered queue and a pending count on the admin console home. Blocked on UW-J24 for the same reason as UW-J29. Wave 2 item 2c of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b blocked UW-J31 The three onboarding interstitials (/guardian/verify, /guardian/awaiting-approval, /guardian/consent) render with no page container: they sit outside GuardianShell in router.tsx, so they inherit none of .guardian-shell__main's padding or max-width, and .console has no rule of its own anywhere in the CSS. The consent page additionally applies guardian-login__field without the cyo-field design-system class that carries the field layout (LoginPage.tsx:461 applies both, which is why only the login page looks right), so it renders with raw browser-default checkboxes and select. The VPC consent screen is the legally load-bearing screen in the product and currently looks like an unstyled prototype. Fix with a minimal OnboardingShell inside the existing GuardianAuthLayout; do not fix it by moving the routes under GuardianShell, which would reintroduce the GET /v1/me dependency those routes' own docstrings explain they must not have (their callers are precisely the users require_principal refuses). Add a visual-regression snapshot for the consent page in the same change. Wave 3 item 3a of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough now unscheduled UW-J32 "New here? Get started" and the Grown-ups door both land on a page headed "Guardian sign-in" whose only kid-facing line ("Ask a grown-up to set up this device for you") is gated behind the intent=authorize-device parameter neither of them carries, so the most inviting link on the landing page, the one written for someone with no account, offers the least guidance to a visitor of any age. The page also never says that "Continue with Google" creates an account, which is the only signup path there is (LoginPage.tsx says so in a comment). Give the new-visitor link its own intent with signup-appropriate copy, carry the grown-ups line into that variant, add a link back to the landing page, and raise the kid-facing line out of the smallest, lowest-contrast slot on a page whose heading and subtitle are both adult-voiced. Wave 4 item 4a of the onboarding overhaul plan. Mostly closed 2026-08-15 by PR #720 (merged as 5f38917), independently of this row. Three of the four asks shipped: the page now says it creates accounts (guardian/loginHeadline.ts's LOGIN_HEADLINE is "Sign in or create your account", plus "New family? Continuing above creates your account." captioning the provider block), it carries a "Back to CYO Adventure" link, and the kid-facing line was raised: under the authorize-device intent it now REPLACES the adult lede rather than sitting beneath it, so it is second in reading order behind the h1 instead of third behind an adult subtitle. The residual is narrower and lower severity than the original row, so read this rather than the paragraph above as the remaining work: a minor who follows a funnel CTA still meets no "this is for grown-ups" signal on the login page itself, because the note is deliberately hidden for the non-intent path (#720's own comment explains why: it is an account-creation prompt, wrong for a child sent to fetch an adult). The landing page's "Grown-ups only, by design" trust card partly covers this, but it sits in funnel stage 3, well below the hero CTA a visitor is most likely to take. Reduced from Medium to Low; overlaps UW-J33, which is the stronger fix for the same reader. registration walkthrough, PR #720 4b unscheduled UW-J33 No age gate of any kind precedes the OAuth button, so a minor can complete sign-in and be provisioned a family and a guardian row before anything asks. Add a plain age affirmation ahead of it, worded as an affirmation and never as verification. Ships regardless of how UW-J25 rules, and becomes the only pre-account check standing if UW-J24 opens the approval gate. Wave 4 item 4b of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b unscheduled UW-J34 ProfileFormDialog.tsx presents seventeen controls at create time where only Name is required, and nothing marks which, so a first-time guardian is asked for sixteen policy decisions before seeing a single story. Every control is a capability somebody asked for (G2 content limits, G3 request permissions, G19 gamification), so the fix is progressive disclosure rather than removal: name and age band up front, the rest behind an "Advanced" section that states the defaults it is applying. Edit mode may stay expanded. Wave 4 item 4c of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b unscheduled UW-J35 Nothing sets the guardian's expectation that a generation and admin review cycle stands between a story request and the shelf, so IntakePage.tsx implies a faster result than the pipeline delivers. Set the expectation at the point of request, and give the empty console a first-run checklist showing the real remaining sequence (profile, device, request, and assign for the cases UW-J01 does not cover). Wave 4 item 4d of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 4b unscheduled UW-J36 frontend/e2e/naive-user/ covers kid, guardian and admin misuse but has no first-run journey spec, which is why a twelve-step flow carrying two blocking gates and one silent required step was found by hand in August rather than by the suite. Add a first-run spec walking the whole path, and add the missing signed-out first-visit scenario to .claude/skills/naive-ux-check/prompts/guardian.md, whose set currently starts from an account that already exists and therefore cannot reach signup, verification, or awaiting-approval at all. Wave 5 of the onboarding overhaul plan. registration walkthrough 5 unscheduled UW-J02 P9 PKCE recovery flow deferred (needs live Supabase) remediation 5 unscheduled UW-J03 P10 cover-staleness escape, blocked on StorybookVersion timestamps remediation 4b blocked UW-J04 P12 schema_version reader gate not started remediation 4b unscheduled UW-J05 P13 durable conflicts store: 409-conflicted writes are currently deleted remediation 5 unscheduled UW-J06 Admin archive and un-publish button: the endpoint exists with no UI persona audit 4b unscheduled UW-J07 Admin resubmit-for-review button; guardian profile-delete button persona audit 4b unscheduled UW-J08 Link request to storybook so "being written" flips; ship the K19 reflect-back or downgrade its DELIVERED status persona audit 4b unscheduled UW-J09 Audit-stamp consistency so self-review is detectable persona audit 5 unscheduled UW-J10 Guardian per-child unassign: merged as PR #428. Verified 2026-07-29: DELETE /storybooks/{storybook_id}/assignments/{profile_id} implemented at api/assignments.py:348-351; capability G8 (capability-register.md) records it delivered 2026-07-27 with the AssignChildrenDialog.tsx Remove control. persona audit 4b done UW-J11 Guardian-defined book groups by age or topic; catalog-trunk-branch admin notification (unresolved); prompt-adjustment suggestions in the dashboard lifecycle redesign 4c unscheduled UW-J12 ADR-015 consent-time budget semantics (quota debit, per-child pre-auth envelopes); the two-step approve-then-publish audit split; family_connections has no consumer widening child visibility authorization matrix 4c unscheduled UW-J13 Authorization matrix missing rows for families, provider-allowlist, moderation-thresholds, and cover-generate traceability doc unscheduled UW-J14 U-5 JIT onboarding admin-seeding footgun is unrecorded in ADR-009 traceability doc unscheduled UW-J15 Plan overclaim (originally raised): roadmap Phase 4b marks G2 controls delivered, but the intake UI hardcodes empty arrays and the profile form lacks a banned-theme field. Verified 2026-08-09 stale: frontend/src/guardian/ProfileFormDialog.tsx has a working banned-themes chip UI, IntakePage.tsx reads the profile's real banned_themes (commented "instead of the previously hardcoded empty list"), and story_requests/brief.py:122 sets content_nogo = list(profile.banned_themes or []). G2 is fully delivered; this row's own overclaim finding was itself incorrect (or the gap it found was fixed without the register being updated). traceability §3.4 now done UW-J16 Track 2 items with no home: web direct billing and the education channel (Android and i18n are already parked) traceability post-launch unscheduled UW-J17 External health check check_external_service is a shipped placeholder that always returns status=True and is not wired into readiness code 5 unscheduled UW-J18 notifications/service.py:25: backfill migration adding pipeline_event.family_id is named as future work code 4c unscheduled UW-J19 covers/storage.py:173: upload cancellation cannot reach a background thread; "tracked as a follow-up, not fixed here" code 5 unscheduled UW-J20 story_requests/service.py:109: a real ledger table is a G13 follow-up once spend needs finer accounting code 8 unscheduled UW-J21 merge_graft_contract and prune_contract are implemented and unit-tested but not wired into the acceptance harness (D7) code content unscheduled UW-J22 review_provider="modal" ships in the config enum but hard-fails at build time; the default "mock" runs no real moderation review code 2b unscheduled UW-J37 P2 dashboard overhaul, deferred by design (D1): finding-first detail-page inversion. The review detail page (ReviewDetailPage.tsx) groups review state by node and severity tier, so a reviewer working one finding cannot see its full context (declared vs. observed intensity, node text, prior disposition) in one place. The 2026-08-25 review-process-hardening plan scoped this out to a follow-on plan rather than building it inline, because today's findings carry no stable identity across a re-moderation run: each moderation_report write replaces the findings array wholesale, so nothing lets a reviewer track "this same finding, seen twice" across reports. The named prerequisite is a finding-identity spec that does not exist yet; write it, then invert the page. review-process-hardening plan 2026-08-25, D1 4b blocked UW-J38 P2 dashboard overhaul, deferred by design (D1): persistent per-finding triage dispositions. The queue has no per-finding triage state (acknowledged, dismissed, escalated) that survives a session or a re-moderation run; the queue's only metric today is the tiered block/flag/advisory counts from the structural collapse (Task 4 of the same plan), not a durable "N unreviewed" count a reviewer could work down across visits. Shares UW-J37's prerequisite: neither can persist a disposition against a finding that has no stable identity across report rewrites, so this is blocked on the same missing finding-identity spec. review-process-hardening plan 2026-08-25, D1 4b blocked UW-J39 P2 dashboard overhaul, deferred by design (D1): declared-vs-observed content-intensity bridging. Nothing in the review UI reconciles the author-declared content flags (violence, scariness, peril, captured at request intake) against what the moderation pipeline actually found in the filled prose. The 2026-08-25 review-process-hardening plan's Task 7 only relabeled the declared flags "Content flags (author-declared)" with a tooltip disclaiming that they are not a moderation verdict, so a reviewer would stop mistaking one for the other; it did not build the comparison. A book whose author declared "mild peril" and whose moderation report found a high-severity violence finding surfaces no mismatch anywhere today. Unlike UW-J37/UW-J38, this does not depend on the finding-identity spec; it is a separate reconciliation feature against existing data. review-process-hardening plan 2026-08-25, D1 4b unscheduled UW-J40 Owner-approved follow-up (ratified 2026-08-25): add an admin-only Remoderate action to the review detail page. ReviewDetailPage.tsx (frontend/src/admin/ReviewDetailPage.tsx) tells a reviewer to ask an operator to remoderate an unusable report, because the admin-only POST /api/v1/admin/remoderate/{storybook_id}/{version} endpoint has no frontend anywhere, discovered during Task 7 of the review-process-hardening plan 2026-08-25. Add the action, enabled when the surface reports report_unusable, calling the existing endpoint directly instead of routing through an operator. Auto-remoderation on an unusable report was considered and rejected: it spends LLM budget without a human decision, and a persistent failure would loop. review-process-hardening plan 2026-08-25 4b unscheduled

docs.title: Cluster K: documentation accuracy and compliance
docs.text:
Stale documentation is directed work: each item below either misleads a reader or misstates the project's own inventory.

ID Item Phase Status UW-K01 Release blocker: docs/known-vulnerabilities.md entries PYSEC-2022-42969 (py, via interrogate 1.7.0) and PYSEC-2026-89 (markdown, CVSS 7.5) are 68 days old with reassessment due 2026-07-20, now 8 days overdue. The OpenSSF release gate blocks releases for any vulnerability older than 60 days regardless of reassessment status. Closed by PR #464 (757ff8e): PYSEC-2022-42969 was withdrawn upstream and PYSEC-2026-89 does not affect the pinned markdown 3.10.2, so neither needed a dependency change. That PR also resolved the release-gate contradiction the entries carried. now done UW-K02 docs/known-vulnerabilities.md: libuuid1 and gawk entries name base image dhi-python:3.12-debian13; the project runs 3.14-debian13. The Review History row is a 2026-MM-DD placeholder and the Resolved Entries table is header-only. DONE 2026-08-16: both entries corrected to 3.14-debian13 (the third 3.12 mention, in the libexpat1 entry, is correct and was left alone: it records an independent cross-check against the 3.12 image). Placeholder replaced with 2026-05-21. The Resolved Entries table has carried six rows since 2026-08-02, so that clause was already stale. Closed by the 2026-08-16 base-image CVE change on branch claude/trivy-base-image-cves-vixpcq: .trivy/ignore-policy.rego (+ trivy.yaml) and the consolidated docs/known-vulnerabilities.md entry. doc done UW-K03 2 fixable linux-libc-dev CVEs due 2026-08-24, blocked on a Renovate digest bump to a base carrying linux-libc-dev 6.12.96-1. DONE: the base reached 6.12.96-1+dhi0 on 2026-07-30, clearing CVE-2026-53399 and CVE-2026-64600; both are in the Resolved Entries table. The row outlived the work it described. 5 done UW-K04 docs/index.md publishes pip install cyo-adventure on the docs home page. This is a deployed app; publish-pypi.yml was deleted. It also claims "Python 3.12+" against >=3.11 and a 3.14 target. now unscheduled UW-K05 TECHNICAL_BASELINE.md "Planned additions" sections list 10 packages as not-yet-added; all 10 shipped long ago. The document reads as a live backlog. now unscheduled UW-K06 TECHNICAL_BASELINE.md: the nginx image is tagged alpine with a note to pin a digest before release. Real supply-chain gap. 5 unscheduled UW-K07 docs/snyk-implementation-findings.md recommendations A through F, including a docs/security/snyk.md that was never written and a decision on Snyk's role against osv-scanner, pip-audit, trivy, bandit, and semgrep. Zero Snyk hits in either master document. 5 decision UW-K08 docs/snyk-implementation-findings.md claims the py transitive dependency "is gone"; uv.lock still carries it via interrogate. Contradicts UW-K01. now unscheduled UW-K09 docs/development/architecture.md lists Authentik as the auth component; auth is Supabase per ADR-009 doc unscheduled UW-K10 docs/architecture/README.md claims "all 21 ADRs"; there are 24. CLAUDE.md says 18. Both understate the decision inventory. now unscheduled UW-K11 docs/api/README.md: the rating upsert update path is not re-exercised in the Postman suite CI hygiene unscheduled UW-K12 data-model.md:380 pipeline_event "will subsume" the current minimal table; data-model.md:446 display_name reserved for a future admin UI doc unscheduled UW-K13 CHANGELOG.md:2727 carries a ## [0.1.0] - TBD placeholder in shipped history doc unscheduled UW-K15 Stale frontmatter on delivered work: ws5, ws7, ws8-floor-recalibration, ws-g-pr3 (25 unchecked boxes despite PR #194), admin-guardian-dual-roles-plan, spec-principal-unresolved-interstitial (shipped as PR #455). condition-evaluator-spec.md is still "Draft" though fully implemented. doc unscheduled UW-K16 The 2026-07-20 roadmap audit calls admin-guardian-dual-roles-plan.md unstarted; the work shipped. Only 3 open decisions remain (admin-only family_id, dual-role guardian widening, role='admin' to 'adult' rename). now decision UW-K17 catalog-first-inventory-gap.md is marked SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28, but Gap B (kid-initiated title requests of existing catalog titles) may not be covered elsewhere doc verify UW-K18 98 RAD markers carry no paired #VERIFY, 82 of them outside tests/. Highest-value: the generation/worker.py concurrency pair, the db/models.py cascade CRITICAL, the classifiers.py API-key placement CRITICAL, and four deploy-ordering CRITICALs in supabase/migrations/. 5 unscheduled UW-K19 tests/CLAUDE.md:22 requires a linked issue on every pytest.mark.skip; only 2 of the declarative marks reference tracked work CI hygiene unscheduled UW-K20 docs/planning/ is the only directory in docs/ exempt from front-matter validation, excluded twice over: the hook's files: ^docs/(?!planning/).*\.md$ regex and a hardcoded skip at tools/validate_front_matter.py:311-322. The cause is that the validator has no schema_type concept and so applies the user-facing-docs schema to everything. Measured 2026-07-28: of 72 planning docs, 2 pass and 241 issues are raised, dominated by three systematic mismatches (planning docs carry an H1 the schema forbids, use status: active against an allowed set of draft/in-review/published, and use tags it does not know). The fix is a planning schema in the validator, not conforming 70 documents to a schema written for a different audience. Until then, scripts/check_work_linkage.py is the only automated gate over docs/planning/. CI hygiene unscheduled UW-K21 No check verifies that an AL-* citation in prose resolves to the lesson it describes. scripts/check_work_linkage.py::_check_lessons_linkage resolves AL-* tokens only where they appear inside cluster C of this register, so a citation anywhere else is never existence-checked and never semantically matched. Found when generation-review-workstream-plan-2026-08-22.md cited AL-551 (the hand-copied-count lesson from PR #738) for the Stage 1 persist-gate defect, which is AL-562 on branch fix/stage1-persist-signal-coupling. Both check_work_linkage.py and check_lessons_log.py passed tree-wide over that document. The same PR's own step-5 acceptance criterion forbids exactly this ("No AL citation in the brief or in code resolves to the wrong row"), so the criterion currently has no enforcer. Proposed: extend the linkage check to resolve every AL-NNN token under docs/ and src/ against the log, erroring on an ID that does not exist and warning where the cited row's Category does not match the citing context. Two lessons from the 2026-08-23 correction pass are held back until PR #742 merges, because the log requires consecutive IDs and #742 holds AL-562..AL-568: (a) an arithmetic identity over two computations proves nothing until both are shown to range over the same set, and (b) a same-day merge can land a review's subject before the review returns. Unblocked 2026-08-23 by PR #742 merging as 37a08a60, which landed AL-562..AL-575 (not AL-568 as estimated above); the two held-back lessons can now be appended above the current maximum. Noted while resolving the id collision this merge produced, and left for that pass rather than written here. doc unscheduled

docs.title: Cluster L: live defects
docs.text:
These are not plan gaps. They are bugs found during the sweep, recorded here only so the register is complete; each is filed as a GitHub issue.

ID Item Issue Status UW-L01 machine.ts:108 wires RESTART to start(story), the new-reader entry point, so a restart on a continuation read reseeds var_state from the book's declared initials and returns to story.start_node, discarding both carried series state and the continuation entry node. Root cause: the machine context keeps only {story, reading, error}, dropping the entryNode/varState pair that ReaderPage.tsx:246 passed to startContinuation, so reset cannot reproduce a continuation even in principle. Canonical across ADR-024's deferred defect, debt SL10, diversity B4, and s5-handoff B4. Fixed in #648: ReaderContext now carries the ContinuationSeed, and both the initial-context factory and reset route through one safeStart(story, continuation?), so a restart reproduces the continuation entry node and carried variables. Scope of the close: the machine can now reproduce a continuation, which is what this row said it could not do "even in principle". The seed is still supplied per session from router location.state, so a reload before the first save loses it; that remainder is tracked as the open half of SL10. #460 done UW-L02 api/get_db_session commits in the teardown half of a yield-dependency, which FastAPI runs after the response is sent, so a client could act on a 201 whose row no other connection could yet see. Was mitigated only by an 1100 ms newman delay that also serves as rate-limit spacing, so it could not be tuned for the race alone. Fixed in #647, split across two layers because neither can see both facts it needs: middleware/unit_of_work.py commits at the ASGI http.response.start message, which is the last moment before any byte reaches the client and the only place where to commit is observable; the dependency keeps the rollback, because it sits inside ExceptionMiddleware and is the only layer that can tell a raised HTTPException(403) from a deliberately returned JSONResponse(404), which is whether to commit. RequestUnitOfWork settles exactly once so whichever half acts first decides. The dependency's commit survives as the fallback for a request that never emits a response start. #461 verify UW-L03 Settings.rate_limit_redis_cooldown_seconds (core/config.py:342, carries a #CRITICAL: timing tag and has unit-test coverage) was never threaded into RateLimitMiddleware, so the middleware fell back to a hardcoded 5.0 and CYO_ADVENTURE_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_COOLDOWN_SECONDS had zero effect in any deployed environment. Found by the 2026-07-31 vulture calibration. Fixed 2026-07-31 in commit bb42b308 (PR #520, "wire the rate-limit Redis knobs and close the UW-F22 dead-symbol findings"): middleware/security.py:933 now passes _settings.rate_limit_redis_cooldown_seconds into the middleware config, alongside the sibling rate_limit_redis_timeout_seconds wiring that was already correct. #516 done UW-L04 The readiness probe is unreachable from outside and returns a hardcoded 200, so it cannot report a database outage. Found 2026-08-04 while executing UW-F17. Every backend router except health declares its own /api/v1 prefix, and frontend/nginx.conf proxies only location /api/. api/health.py declares APIRouter(prefix="/health"), which is outside that prefix, so FastAPI's liveness and readiness handlers are not reachable through the ingress at all: /api/health/live returns a JSON 404 from FastAPI. Worse, the same nginx config defines location /health { return 200 'OK'; } for the frontend container's own probe, which shadows the path completely, so GET https://cyo.williamshome.family/health/ready answers with a two-byte text/plain OK from nginx (with a duplicated Content-Type header and server: nginx) while the readiness logic never executes. The consequence is not cosmetic: readiness is the check that proves database connectivity, so any external uptime monitor pointed at that URL reports healthy with the database completely down, and the R1 checklist recorded a "verified live 2026-07-07: both 200" pass on exactly that anti-oracle. /api/v1/me correctly returns 401 application/json, confirming the proxy itself is fine and the fault is the prefix mismatch plus the shadowing stub. Fixed 2026-08-04, not by the rename this row originally proposed. A rename alone would have caused an outage: the production backend healthcheck is defined out-of-repo in homelab-infra services/cyo-adventure/docker-compose.yml, probes /health/live, exits non-zero on any status >= 400, and is wired to depends_on: condition: service_healthy, so this repo deploying ahead of that one would have marked the container unhealthy rather than merely mis-pathed. Delivered additively instead: app.py mounts the health router twice, /api/v1/health/* as the canonical schema-visible form and /health/* as a schema-hidden alias, with the alias's retirement precondition recorded in a #CRITICAL marker at the mount site. middleware/security.py widened its HTTPS-redirect exemption to both prefixes, since a missed prefix there surfaces as a 307 that a probe reads as a failure, not as a 404. frontend/nginx.conf narrows its own stub to location = /nginx-health and, critically, returns an explicit 404 for /health rather than deleting the block: deleting it would let the path fall through to the SPA try_files fallback and answer 200 text/html, which is the same false pass wearing a different hat. Every probe in this repo (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, frontend/e2e-real/real-stack.ts, runbook section 3) now asserts content-type: application/json, so a static stub cannot forge a pass. #609 done UW-L05 Production holds a family row with no users and no contents. Found 2026-08-04 while executing UW-F17 section 6, which needed the real family inventory to tell a genuine isolation check from a vacuous one. Production has three family rows: 3a152319 (the real family, 2 profiles, 6 assignments, 1 story request, 5 device grants, 3 reading states), 84b96700 (the E2E test family, 1 profile, 5 assignments, 4 grants, 0 story requests, 0 reading states), and 0ca7a109, which has zero profiles, zero assignments, zero grants, zero requests, zero reading states, and zero user rows pointing at it. A family with no users is unreachable by design: every adult route resolves the caller's family through their user row, so nothing can read or write it and no console surface will ever list it. That is why it is recorded rather than urgent. It matters anyway for two reasons. First, guardian accounts are created by an empty POST /v1/onboarding (there is no signup form), so a family row with no user is the exact residue a partially-failed JIT provisioning would leave, and if that is the cause then the write is not atomic and a real guardian could hit it. Second, it inflates every family-count assertion, so a test that asserts "2 families" against production is already wrong and a test that asserts "3" encodes the anomaly as expected. To do: establish provenance before touching it, by checking whether created_at lines up with a known onboarding attempt or with an early manual seed, then either make the onboarding write atomic (transaction spanning family + user insert) or record it as a one-off seed artifact. Do not delete the row as the first action: while it exists it is the only evidence of how it came to exist. Re-checked 2026-08-08: a fourth family appeared, and it is the more informative of the two. adb9e257, created 2026-08-05 01:07 UTC, has zero profiles, assignments, grants, requests and reading states, but one guardian user row, unlike 0ca7a109's zero. That difference decides the provenance question this row was opened to answer: an empty family plus a user is what a completed empty onboarding leaves behind, whereas a family with no user is what a failed one leaves behind. So the two rows are probably not the same event, and the atomicity concern applies only to 0ca7a109. Check whether adb9e257's single user is a real person or a test sign-in before concluding either way; if it is real, the finding is a guardian who onboarded and never created a profile, which is a product observation rather than a defect. The real family also gained a third child profile in the same window, so both counts this register and the R1 checklist pin assertions to have now moved. Anything asserting a family count or a profile count against live production needs re-deriving; see the drift note in the checklist's Section 6. (no issue) unscheduled UW-L06 Retire the un-prefixed /health/* alias. app.py mounts the health router twice, /api/v1/health/* as the canonical schema-visible form and /health/* as a schema-hidden alias; the alias exists only so the out-of-repo production healthcheck keeps passing across the deploy. UW-L04 recorded the retirement precondition in a #CRITICAL marker at the mount site but scheduled no work to act on it, so a permanent second mount entered the codebase with a retirement plan nothing tracks. Raised in review of #609. Open prerequisite, and the reason this is blocked rather than unscheduled: homelab-infra services/cyo-adventure/docker-compose.yml probes /health/live, exits non-zero on any status >= 400, and is wired to depends_on: condition: service_healthy, so it must be repointed at /api/v1/health/live and redeployed before the alias is dropped. Dropping it first marks the container unhealthy rather than merely mis-pathed, which is the same outage the additive fix in UW-L04 was chosen to avoid. Retirement is then three deletions plus their tests: the second include_router call in app.py, the /health entry in _HEALTH_PATH_PREFIXES (middleware/security.py), and the location /health 404 block in frontend/nginx.conf, whose explicit 404 exists only to stop the SPA try_files fallback answering 200 text/html on the alias path. TestLegacyHealthPathAlias (tests/unit/test_app.py) and frontend/e2e-prod/health-probe.spec.ts both assert the alias's present behaviour, so they must be inverted rather than deleted; otherwise the retirement is assumed instead of proven. Also repoint the frontend container's out-of-repo external prober, which frontend/Dockerfile documents as curling bare /health and which this repo now answers with a 404 by design. #609 blocked UW-L07 Guardian profile resolution runs before the RLS context it depends on, so every guardian in production sees zero profiles. Found 2026-08-08 while executing UW-F17 against revision 631c0d8a (v0.68.0). api/deps.py::require_principal calls _resolve_profiles (line ~545) roughly 36 lines before apply_family_rls_context (line ~581). _resolve_profiles selects from child_profile, an ADR-022 Tier 1 family_scoped table whose policy is family_id::text = current_setting('app.family_id', true) OR current_setting('app.is_admin', true) = 'true'. With the GUC unset, current_setting(..., true) returns NULL, the predicate is unsatisfiable, and the read returns zero rows, so principal.profile_ids is empty for every guardian. GET /v1/profiles then short-circuits on it (api/profiles.py ~374) and the console renders "No profiles yet" over a family that has three children. This fails closed: it is an outage of the profiles surface, not a data leak, and the underlying rows are intact. Confirmed live: the 2026-08-07 e2e-prod run captured GET /api/v1/me returning "profile_ids":[] and GET /api/v1/profiles returning {"profiles":[]} while the database held the profiles. Why it stayed invisible until now: RLS never applies to a table's owner, so before the ADR-021 cutover the API connected as postgres and the policy was inert; cutting over to cyo_api (rolbypassrls=false) is what activated the ordering bug. Any bug of this shape is undetectable pre-cutover, which argues for testing as the non-owner role rather than for testing more. It is a recurrence, not a novel defect: _device_principal (defined at deps.py ~625) already applies the context before its Tier 1 reads and carries a #CRITICAL comment naming the identical staging outage of 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-02; that fix was applied to the device branch only. Sharper still, the file states the false invariant in its own words, one call site away from the bug. Two #CRITICAL blocks assert exactly what _resolve_profiles falsifies: the block above the apply_family_rls_context call (deps.py ~570) reasons that "two of the three branches resolve without needing the context this sets: guardian/admin read the user row just above under the Tier 2 blanket policy", and the block inside _device_principal (deps.py ~674) states that device_grant "is the ONLY pre-principal read of one". Both are false the moment _resolve_profiles reads child_profile at line ~545. The fix must correct these two comments as well, or the codebase keeps asserting a disproven invariant beside the corrected code, which is how the device-only half fix survived review the first time. Coverage gap that let it ship: tests/integration/test_rls_tier1_enforcement.py covers the device branch (test_device_principal_resolves_under_tier1_rls) with no guardian equivalent exercising the real require_principal path as cyo_api. Second-order finding, worth fixing with it: the cross-family isolation test (frontend/e2e-prod/guardian-books-and-isolation.spec.ts ~184) asserts the E2E family sees zero story requests; story_request is family_scoped too, so under this defect that assertion is satisfied by the bug, with its rendered-heading positive control fully intact. Only the profiles half, which expects a non-zero count, catches the failure. An emptiness assertion over a Tier 1 table needs a non-empty companion assertion under the same policy; a rendered-heading control proves the page loaded, never that scoping ran. Fix: apply the context before _resolve_profiles, keeping the existing later call, correct the two #CRITICAL comments above, and add the missing guardian regression test at the require_principal level rather than at the query level. Status caveat: PR #641 is open and implements exactly this fix over the same two files, so if it merges before this row does, the unscheduled status and the Fix paragraph are already historical; the deployed claims above stay accurate either way, since they are conditioned on production serving the fix rather than on the fix merging. #639 unscheduled UW-L08 Two published books, sk_vault_of_nine_iron (block/high, drowning) and sk_ninth_hand (flag/high, suicidal intent), hold severe-finding moderation reports and must be re-moderated once feat/moderation-review-hardening deploys. The 2026-08-25 review-process-hardening plan's D4 gate named both from its ground-truth section, which recorded sk_ninth_hand specifically as untracked anywhere; this row is now the tracking item for both books. The plan's Task 13 was to re-moderate both under the current pipeline after Tasks 1-10 deploy and put the fresh reports in front of the owner via the reviewer SOP's escalation section. Task 13 never ran in this execution: it depends on a deploy that has not happened, and no Task 13 brief was written (only Task 12's ops-sweep brief exists in .superpowers/sdd/). Owner to rule: the project owner, on unpublish-or-keep for each book once its fresh report is in hand (an owner-only content call per D4); both books stay published until then. Sequencing ratified 2026-08-25: no precautionary unpublish; after the branch deploys, re-moderate these two books first as targeted --book-id runs, review the fresh reports per the reviewer SOP's escalation section and make the D4 call per book, then run the full backfill sweep (runbook section 8). Scheduled-check posture ratified 2026-08-25: .github/workflows/moderation-report-health.yml's Monday cron stays running rather than being disabled or loosened; a red run every Monday until the 12 in-review books AL-624 records are re-moderated is an accepted, expected forcing function, not a defect in the check or its schedule. (This row's own two published books carry genuine block/high findings, not fail-safe artifacts, so moderation_report_unusable() does not flag them; they stay tracked here rather than by that workflow.) The workflow now carries the same cron-posture decision in a comment at its own file. (no issue) decision

docs.title: Cluster M: external and owner-gated
docs.text:
Work this repository cannot complete on its own.

ID Item Owner Status UW-M01 Deploy the device-grant RLS fix to :staging once it merges, then re-run e2e-staging.yml to confirm the tier is green. Fully re-diagnosed 2026-08-02; the original "rebuild the stale :staging image from b29aa6b" ask is refuted. That premise fails two ways: every migration since b29aa6b is purely additive (no DROP/RENAME COLUMN), so a forward-migrated database cannot break older ORM code, and trigger-image-build.yml has succeeded on every merge through 2026-08-02. The tier's redness was two independent faults. (1) Three deterministic 500s (/v1/notifications, /v1/review-queue, /v1/guardian/books, the only three routes issuing a full-ORM select(Storybook)/select(StorybookVersion)) caused by the 07-30 migration stall, i.e. the database being BEHIND a current backend, the exact inverse of the original diagnosis. Fixed by repair run 30754078625, confirmed in run 30757075720. (2) The device-grant 401: api/deps.py::_device_principal reads select(DeviceGrant).where(jti == ...) to learn the grant's family_id, but device_grant is an ADR-022 Tier 1 family_scoped table and apply_family_rls_context only runs AFTER the principal is built, so the lookup runs with app.family_id unset, matches zero rows fail-closed exactly as 20260724120000_scoped_rls_tier1_family_scoping.sql documents, and is reported as "device grant token failed verification". Not a secret, not a deployment fact: docker logs proves the SAME container minted (201) and rejected (401) in the same second. The comment at deps.py:571 claims there is no chicken-and-egg, which holds for guardian/admin (the user table has a Tier 2 blanket policy) and for child (no DB read at all) but was never extended to the device branch, the only pre-principal read of a Tier 1 table. Latent since the 2026-07-18 Tier 1 cutover and invisible to every other tier because local and e2e-real-* connect as the owner, which bypasses RLS. Code fix is in this repo on fix/device-grant-rls-lookup: _device_principal now applies the RLS context itself, from the token's already-verified family_id claim, before the lookup. A SECURITY DEFINER bypass function was drafted first and discarded: it would have made app code depend on a migration-only database object (absent from the ORM create_all test fixtures) and could not deploy until that migration landed, reintroducing the very migrate-before-deploy ordering hazard that caused fault (1) above. Setting context from the claim needs no migration, deploys as pure code, and additionally binds the grant row to the family the token claims, which the jti-only lookup never checked. This row covers only the owner-side deploy and re-run that follows. homelab-infra unscheduled UW-M02 Naive-user session with real children. Gates UW-I01, UW-I02, and 15 unrun Track B scenarios. project owner blocked UW-M03 Counsel engagement: ADR-018 D1-D5, ADR-016 ring-2 granularity, ADR-023 OD-1 and OD-5. Long lead time; the roadmap already flags that this should start now. Updated 2026-08-06: the ADR-018 leg is packaged and ready to send. Every owner-side prerequisite is closed (D2 child-directed, D4 owner-drafts/counsel-reviews plus Safe Harbor sequenced counsel-first, D5 corpus constraint, all recorded in the ADR 2026-08-06; D1 and D3 were already decided), both rule-mandated D4 artifacts exist (information-security-program.md published, data-retention-policy.md drafted 2026-08-06), and the packet is assembled at counsel-engagement-brief.md. Note the row covers D1-D5 now, not D1-D4: D5 (AI-training consent segregation) was added to the ADR 2026-08-01 and this row predated it. What remains is purely external: retain counsel and get rulings. The ADR-016 and ADR-023 legs are untouched by this update and remain unpackaged. project owner decision UW-M04 OpenRouter DPA execution (privacy-model Blocker 1a) project owner decision UW-M05 Wyrmreach provenance conflict: the series design and report live only on unmerged branch claude/dnd-story-game-series-mqr9zy with unsigned commits, and no data/series/wyrmreach/ exists on main, yet the series is recorded as live in production. Resolve how published content reached production without a main merge before doing more Wyrmreach work. project owner decision UW-M06 Owner decisions from the authoring handoff: book 2 shape, Wyrmreach doc placement, the reader-path four, and whether PL-17's floor applies to gamebooks. Standing alternative: retire the brass-lantern series. project owner decision UW-M07 R2 cover bucket is publicly served, contradicting the code's own invariant. covers/storage.py asserts as #CRITICAL: security that the bucket must have no public custom domain or r2.dev access bound to it, because covers are served only as short-lived presigned GET URLs. It did. Verified 2026-07-28: GET https://cyo-bucket.williamshome.family/sk_ashfall_expedition/1.webp returned 200 image/webp, 86,732 bytes, with no credentials. Because cover_object_key is deterministic ({storybook_id}/{version}.webp), anyone who could guess a storybook id could read any cover, including one still at pending_review under the H2 approval gate shipped in PR #469, so that gate bound the API read paths only. Fix was unbinding the public custom domain in the Cloudflare dashboard, outside this repository. Resolved 2026-07-30: the project owner disconnected the custom domain and cleared the DNS record; re-verified this session with dig cyo-bucket.williamshome.family failing to resolve (Could not resolve host) against a working general-egress sanity check (curl https://example.com returned 200 from the same environment), so the negative is genuine, not a local network gap. The bucket is no longer reachable at that hostname at all; the H2 cover gate is again a real reachability control, not only an API-surface one. project owner done UW-M08 ADR-022 Tier 1 RLS is inert on production. The prod backend connects as postgres.cvrnaydpzijtszfbsraq, and the postgres role has rolbypassrls = true (verified against the prod database 2026-08-02), so every family_scoped policy created by 20260724120000_scoped_rls_tier1_family_scoping.sql is bypassed and the family-isolation backstop enforces nothing in production. The least-privilege roles the migration was written for (cyo_api, cyo_worker, both rolbypassrls = false) already EXIST on the prod project but are unused by the API. Staging is correctly cut over to cyo_api, which is the only reason UW-M01's device-grant defect surfaced at all: prod cannot fail that way because it enforces no policy. Remedy is the ADR-021 least-privilege cutover on prod, pointing the backend at cyo_api and the worker at cyo_worker. Do NOT cut over until UW-M01's code fix has merged and been verified on staging, or the same device-grant 401 will land on production the moment the role changes. Resolved 2026-08-04, closed by the same cutover as UW-A03: the precondition (PR #560 merged and green on staging) was satisfied before the production role switch, so the family-isolation backstop is now enforced live, not just present in migrations. homelab-infra done UW-M09 Revoke the exposed OpenRouter API key. The key value was echoed into the 2026-08-20 session transcript by a shell-expansion mistake during an env check, so the credential stays usable until revoked. Revoke at openrouter.ai, create a replacement, update the environment variable, and record completion in handoff-modal-deepseek-v4-smoke-test-2026-08-20.md. Only the account holder can revoke it. Note this repository is PUBLIC, so the handoff recording the exposure is itself published; that raises the urgency rather than changing the remedy. project owner unscheduled UW-M10 Stop the stuck DeepSeek V4 Pro Modal endpoint. Endpoint ep-k7GKhWPbAoEy4PZ19TvKXf never left "Starting up" (8 GPUs could not be provisioned) and keeps retrying provisioning, which bills without ever serving. Stop it in the Modal dashboard. Recorded in handoff-modal-deepseek-v4-smoke-test-2026-08-20.md. project owner unscheduled UW-M11 Rename the Modal proxy-token env vars in the remote environment configuration. The pair is present as MODAL_KEY and MIDAL_SECRET (note the MIDAL typo); core/config.py::Settings reads MODAL_PROXY_KEY / MODAL_PROXY_SECRET, so no code-level Modal test can authenticate until they are renamed. Values load only at container start, so the rename needs a fresh session to take effect. Lives in the Claude environment configuration, outside this repository. Recorded in handoff-modal-deepseek-v4-smoke-test-2026-08-20.md. project owner unscheduled UW-M12 DeepSeek V4 Pro as a Modal container, not a managed endpoint. The managed-endpoint route is ruled out: it needs 8 GPUs this workspace cannot allocate (verified 2026-08-21 over 15+ minutes of authenticated 503s). The remaining option is a custom app deployment like the earlier cyo-standard one. Blocked on GPU capacity or quota for the required instance class, which is a Modal-side constraint. Transport, auth, and response shape are already proven against the shared Kimi-K3 endpoint, so capacity is the remaining deployment blocker; adapter work in UW-F44 is still required before real use. Evidenced in handoff-modal-deepseek-v4-smoke-test-2026-08-20.md. project owner blocked

docs.title: Cluster N: external scope-comparison findings
docs.text:
Sourced from a 2026-08-05 comparison of three externally-authored, LLM-generated planning documents (a project scope, a product/requirements document, and a commercial/revenue viability report, all produced from a one-paragraph description with no visibility into this repository) against the live project. Most of what those documents assumed was either already decided differently here or is irrelevant to this project's actual delivery model; these rows are the concrete mechanics and reference material worth retaining. Full detail, citations, and field-level tables for each row live in external-scope-comparison-2026-08-05.md, since the source .docx files themselves live outside this repository and are not expected to persist. Each row below restates enough of that document to be actionable on its own, which means the same claim is written twice; the comparison document is authoritative on any conflict, and a correction to a row's reasoning belongs there first.

ID Item Phase Status UW-N01 Adopt the external document's append-only entitlement-ledger design (grant/reserve/release/consume/expire/reverse events, never a mutable balance) as the starting design for commerce once Phase 8 (Capacitor + IAP) begins. No payment-processing or entitlement-ledger implementation exists in this repository today. Further informed by the companion Commercial and Revenue Viability Report's offer ladder ($9.99 one-time / $9.99 monthly / $69.99-79.99 annual test) and $0.90 per-story direct-cost stack. 8 unscheduled UW-N02 Feed ADR-018's still-open VPC method decision with the external document's cited sources (FTC COPPA Rule 90 FR 16918, codified at 16 CFR Part 312, effective 2025-06-23 with a general compliance date of 2026-04-22 that has already passed as of 2026-08-05; ROSCA; Oregon ORS 646A.293-295 and 646A.570-589) and its required consent-record field list. Decision, not implementation; waits on the counsel engagement UW-M03 already names. Updated 2026-08-06: the citations above are now carried into counsel-engagement-brief.md, which puts them to counsel marked as unverified-by-us and asks counsel to confirm them against the Federal Register text rather than relying on this repository's secondary sourcing. That is the ADR's own stated caveat, so the row's remaining work is counsel's ruling, not further internal sourcing. The consent-record field list is still worth checking against the shipped consent_* columns once counsel confirms which fields are required. 7 decision UW-N03 Replace the hardcoded CLOSED_VOCABULARIES dict (storybook/personalization_values.py) with a versioned, schema-pinned VariableDefinition-style registry, so a historical story renders reproducibly after the variable catalog changes shape. Blocked on the same ADR-023 Stage A G1 STOP that blocks UW-H01: do not start ahead of that re-plan. 4b blocked UW-N04 Widen the axe-core e2e a11y suite's tag scope from WCAG 2.1 AA (wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa) to WCAG 2.2 by adding both wcag22a and wcag22aa: axe's WCAG tags are additive per level, so wcag22aa alone covers only the 2.2 Level AA additions and would silently skip the Level A ones, consistent help (3.2.6) and redundant entry (3.3.7), which are the two criteria most relevant to consent and rights flows. In scope at AA: target size minimum (2.5.8), focus not obscured minimum (2.4.11), dragging movements (2.5.7), accessible authentication minimum (3.3.8). Out of scope for an AA target: 2.4.12 focus not obscured enhanced and 2.4.13 focus appearance, both AAA. Matches the external document's NFR-A11Y-01 baseline. Updated 2026-08-11: WCAG 2.2 scanning (both wcag22a and wcag22aa, exactly as this row specifies) now runs, but on the new weekly accessibility-compliance-weekly.yml job (ADR-029) rather than the per-PR gate, so this row is not closed. The owner ruled the per-PR frontend-e2e job should not grow scope or run time; widening the blocking gate itself, if ever wanted, is still this row's open work. 5 unscheduled UW-N05 Decide, before Track 2 phases 6-9 open intake to outside families, whether to keep ADR-005's admin-only-approves-every-story model or move to the external document's guardian-primary-approval-with-staff-escalation model. Admin-only review does not scale headcount-wise to a multi-family product; the alternative is only as safe as the moderation-calibration work already tracked under GS2/GS3. Owner to rule: the project owner, jointly with whoever holds the safety-operator role at the time. 7 decision UW-N06 Pin an ASVS level and a penetration-test surface list onto the ASVS 5.0.0 spine that docs/security/assurance-spine.md already names as the primary application-security framework, using the external document's NFR-SEC-01/NFR-SEC-16 target of Level 2 and its surface list (guardian/child/admin, API authorization, tenant isolation, payment/entitlement, export and deletion, AI-specific abuse) as the candidate scope statement for Phase 5's engagement (Cluster E). Do not adopt NFR-SEC-12's OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications as a control catalog: assurance-spine.md already classifies it, the API Top 10, and MITRE ATLAS as threat enumeration for corpus building, with the explicit note "Not control catalogs. Do not spine on them." Scoping refinement of an existing decision only; the actual gap closure is the existing Cluster E rows. 5 unscheduled UW-N07 Reconcile the external document's planning-default retention table against the already-resolved category-by-category schedule in docs/compliance/coppa-gdpr-remediation-plan.md ("Resolved 2026-07-20: accepted as drafted", kept as the actual policy and cited by ADR-018), rather than drafting from scratch: adopt the categories the resolved schedule omits (adult account/household, consent evidence, product analytics, application logs, financial records, backups), and settle the one row where the two disagree, reading progress, resolved as "life of the active profile plus 30-90 days after deactivation" against the external default of "target 12 months' inactivity." The resolved policy governs until deliberately changed. Owners to rule on the newly added categories: privacy counsel and finance. Feeds the same ADR-018 gate as UW-N02. Updated 2026-08-06: the reconciliation is done; the rulings are not. data-retention-policy.md now exists as the retention artifact ADR-018 D4 requires, drafted 2026-08-06 and still status: draft rather than published. It reproduces the 2026-07-20 resolved schedule verbatim rather than re-deriving it, settles the reading-progress row in favour of the resolved policy ("life of the active profile plus 30-90 days after deactivation" governs over the external 12-month-inactivity default), and adds all six omitted categories. Three of the added categories carry no window and are written as "Not yet set, owner ruling required" rather than being given an invented number: consent evidence, product analytics, and application logs. Financial records is marked not-applicable today (no payment data is collected) and needs a ruling before any payment feature ships. This row stays decision because those rulings are the remaining work. 7 decision UW-N08 ADR-027 decision 5's automated image-moderation classifier (the precondition for expanding per-node art past the seven-skeleton pilot) has no register home; its own text says only "tracked as follow-on work," which is the unscheduled-deferral pattern this register exists to close. Found while backfilling ADR-027's required Follow-on work section. Open prerequisite: the seven-skeleton pilot must run and its results must justify scaling before the classifier is worth building, which is why ADR-027's follow-on section calls this "blocked in effect on the pilot's own results per decision 5." 4b blocked UW-N09 Cite the Commercial and Revenue Viability Report's generated-image cost estimate (8-12 scenes ≈ $0.27-$2.40/story, public per-image rates) in ADR-027, whose own budget section priced storage and delivery only, never generation spend. Done: landed in ADR-027's new Follow-on work section in PR #620, the same change that added the comparison document. The figure is a per-story total derived from public per-image rates, not a per-image price, and it carries a scale caveat: 8-12 scenes is the external document's assumption, while ADR-027's own pilot scope is 10-45 node images per book, so it must be re-derived against 10-45 before informing any expand decision. 4b done UW-N10 Adopt the Commercial and Revenue Viability Report's "30-day Family Story Value Rate" north-star metric and its anti-gaming metric definitions (a completion requires a validated ending, not scrolling; a replay requires a deliberate alternate-path pick, not an accidental reload; unit cost includes support minutes) as this project's engagement/analytics measurement framework. Unblocked by commerce: no equivalent event-taxonomy or KPI doc exists in docs/planning/ today, and the framework is usable at the current family-tier, pre-monetization scale. 4c unscheduled
